AppliedLimit.description:
A Limit that applies to a Run (ADRs 0041 and 0101): its scope's kind and

ArtifactId.description: Which Pinned artifact: its kind, its name and its build.

oneOf.description: A browser build, such as Chrome for Testing's.
Playwright's driver (ADR 0019).
The versioned copy of an executable a Daemon runs from (ADR 0024).

A full Clean-up rules set (ADR 0047).
Recorded mouse movements (ADR 0035).

Asked.description: The format, with its default options.

entries.description:
Every entry the log holds, in sequence, each with its hash: the

How many entries the log holds.

first_broken.description:

intact.description:
Whether every entry chains to the one before it and the head file

AxisReason.description: One reason a Run is not `verified` or not `complete` (ADR 0029).

call_id.description:
The AI task it is about, by its `callId`, when it is about one (ADR

code.description:
What it is, such as `stopped` or `failed`; a reason this reader does

count.description:

the pages left at a Block cause, or the requests a stop left.

BodyHandle.description: A page body as a handle: its ID, the file that holds it and its size.

body.description: Its ID, the lowercase hex SHA-256 of its bytes.

path.description: The file that holds it, which a Client on the same machine reads.

run_id.description: The Run whose folder holds it.

closed.description:

person.description: Whom the stopping Client acts for (ADR 0031), when known.

CancelledBy.description:
Who stopped a call that `call_cancelled` ended (ADR 0113): the

oneOf.description: A person, through a Client that acts for them (ADR 0031).
Another Client, such as through `$/cancel`.
The program, closing a parent value from another task or thread.

The browser, outside every Client: a page's window closed there, or
the browser quit.

CertificatePin.description:
One pin of the known-certificates store, as `certs.list` answers it and
as the store's rows hold it: a host whose certificate was accepted on
first use, and the key it must keep presenting.

changed_spki_sha256.description:
The SHA-256 of the key the host presented instead, which stopped it
with `certificate_changed`, as `sha256/` and its standard base64: the
key `certs.accept` pins in its place. None while no change waits.

host.description: The host, as the URL parser leaves it.

pinned_at.description: When it was pinned; none when the row cannot be read.

run_id.description:
The Run whose connection pinned it; none outside a Run or when the
row cannot be read.

spki_sha256.description:
The SHA-256 of the pinned certificate's `SubjectPublicKeyInfo`, as
`sha256/` and its standard base64; none when the row cannot be read,
which stops the host as a changed key.

CertsAcceptParams.description:
What `certs.accept` takes: the host, and the changed key the person
accepts, as `certs.list` shows it.

host.description: The pinned host, as the URL parser leaves it.

spki_sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the changed key, as `sha256/` and its standard base64.

host.description: The pinned host, as the URL parser leaves it.

forgotten.description: Whether the caller had a pin for it, now removed.

Checkpoint.description:
A Checkpoint as the engine reports it (ADRs 0002, 0102 and 0116): a
consistent, self-contained copy of a Run's state, complete at its
location before it is reported, from which the Run resumes on this
machine or another one.

digest.description: The SHA-256 of its bytes, in lowercase hexadecimal.

journal_position.description:
The position of the run's journal it holds: how many commits of the
run file it contains. A resume from it redoes the work after.

location.description: Where it is: the file's path on the engine's machine.

run_epoch.description:
The run epoch of the writer that took it (ADR 0003), which a
destination compares and sets: one older than it holds is refused.

Claim.description:
What a model said of the work it was given (ADR 0100): a signal, never
proof.

oneOf.description: It said it was done.

It said it gave up, which stops the work with the reason `gave_up`
(ADR 0117).

ClickParams.description: What `locator.click` takes: the locator whose element it clicks.

ClosedValue.description:
What was closed or stopped under a call that `call_cancelled` ended
(ADR 0113), open (ADR 0079).

oneOf.description: Its page.
Its page's Session.
Its page's browser.
Its Run, stopped.
Its Connection.

Completeness.description:
Whether a Run's results cover everything in its scope (ADRs 0005 and
0029).

oneOf.description: They do.
The Run ended early.
It finished, but the engine cannot vouch that nothing was missed.

keys.description:
The keys to explain, each a key or a prefix of keys, such as
`timeout`; every key when empty.

missing_project.description:
The path of the project configuration the Client was named, in place
of `project`, when no file is there: it sets nothing, and the answer
lists it as not found.

origin.description:
Where those run values come from: a scope's `settings` option by
default, or the CLI's flags when the CLI asks a Daemon.

project.description: The project configuration to explain with.

run_id.description:
The Run ID of a live Run to explain, with the settings it opened
with; none explains the Connection's own, the run values given set
over them (ADR 0083). One that is no Run ID fails with
`run_id_invalid`, and one given with `settings`, `origin`,
`project` or `missing_project` with `invalid_params`.

settings.description:
Run-layer values to explain with, as a Run's `settings` would give
them.

added.description:
Whether it was added: false when user configuration listed it
already, which then changed nothing and recorded nothing.

domain.description: The domain, as `consent.domains` now lists it.

warning.description:
What the person takes on, in plain words, as the person surface showed it
beside the answer and the Audit log records it.

ConsoleLocation.description:
Where a console message was written: its script's URL and position, as
the browser counts them from 0.

url.description: The script's URL; empty for a script the page evaluated.

ConsoleMessage.description: What `page.console` reports: a message the page wrote to its console.

text.description:
Its text: each argument, a primitive as its value and any other as
the browser describes it, joined by spaces.

type.description:
Its type as Playwright names it, such as `log`, `warning` or
`error`.

Contacts.description: The contacts the page shows, each value once, where it first appears.

emails.description:
Its e-mail addresses, from `mailto:` links and from text matching
the HTML Standard's valid e-mail address syntax.

phones.description: Its telephone numbers, from `tel:` links and from text.

social.description: Its social profiles, from links to the extractor's list of networks.

Count.description:
A count of matches, bounded on either side or both: an exact count is
both bounds.

max.description: The most; no bound when absent.

min.description: The fewest; no bound when absent.

Counted.description: What `locator.wait_for_count` answers: how many elements matched.

CpuReading.description: The engine's CPU and Tokio workers, as the governor read them.

busy.description:
The engine's CPU time since the last sample, in percent of its
allowance.

parallelism.description:
How many threads the engine may run at once, its CPU allowance
(`available_parallelism`, which honours a cgroup's quota).

tokio_busy.description: The Tokio workers' busy time since the last sample, in percent.

DaemonEndpoint.description:

0024): a `0600` Unix socket on macOS and Linux, loopback TCP on
Windows.

A loopback address and port.

DaemonHealth.description:
What `daemon.health` answers: what the ops listener's `/livez` and
`/readyz` check (ADR 0050). In a Daemon group, readiness ignores the
Lead Daemon's reachability.

live.description:
Whether it is live: its runtime and its Runs' registry, which writes
their run state, respond.

ready.description: Whether it is ready: live, and able to take a new Run.

unready.description: Why it is not ready, when it is not; empty when it is.

DaemonState.description: What `daemon.status` answers: the running Daemon's state.

clients.description: How many Clients are connected, the caller included.

heap.description:
Its live heap: the bytes its own allocations hold now, as its
executable's allocator counts them, without the pages that
allocator keeps once they are freed; none where nothing counts
them.

kept_alive.description:
Whether it never stops idle: `--keep-alive`, a held Schedule or an
installed service.

live_runs.description: How many of its Runs are live.

product.description: The Product the Daemon runs as.

DaemonStopping.description: What `daemon.stop` answers, before the Daemon stops.

live_runs.description: How many live Runs it stops, each resumable from its own state.

Dialog.description: A dialog as its handler sees it.

default_value.description: A prompt's default value; empty for any other kind.

DialogAcceptParams.description: What `dialog.accept` takes: the dialog, and a prompt's text.

prompt_text.description: The text a prompt returns; its default value when absent.

DialogAnswered.description: What an answer to a dialog answers once the page closed the dialog.

DialogHandleParams.description:
What `dialog.handle` gives the handler: the dialog, named by the ID its
answer passes.

dialog_id.description: The dialog, which an answer names.

id.description: The id of the `page.on_dialog` call whose handler is asked.

What the handler replies to `dialog.handle` once it ended; a failure
reply says it failed.

DialogId.description: One dialog a handler answers, which `dialog.*` names.

DialogType.description: A dialog's kind, as Playwright's `dialog.type()` names it.

DialogsEnded.description: What `page.on_dialog` answers when its page closes.

A Download of a Run, named by the engine when it keeps its file:

total_bytes.description: The bytes the answer announced, when it did.

path.description:
The program's path, absolute, which an Attached engine writes
itself; any other engine leaves it to the SDK and sends the file's
bytes instead.

DownloadSaved.description: What `download.save_as` answers once the file is whole.

sha256.description: The SHA-256 of its bytes, in lowercase hexadecimal.

written.description:
Whether the engine wrote the program's path itself; when not, the
`$/chunk` notifications before this answer carried every byte, and
the SDK writes the path.

EffectAttempt.description:
The crawl attempt an Effect is declared through: a handler's `ctx.run`,
which is bound to its attempt (ADR 0093).

crawl_request_id.description: The ID of the crawl request whose attempt declares the Effect.

lease_epoch.description: The attempt's lease epoch, as `crawl_request.handle` gave it.

EffectCloseParams.description:
What `effect.close` takes: the entry `effect.open` answered and how its
body ended.

run_id.description: The Run whose Effect journal keeps the Effect.

EffectClosed.description:
What `effect.close` answers: how the engine judged the body by what it
sent for it.

oneOf.description:
The body returned a value the Effect journal keeps: it never runs
again under its key, and the SDK answers `performed`.

The body did not return, and nothing was sent or the Effect is
repeatable: the entry is dropped, the SDK propagates the body's
error, and the next declaration runs the body.

sent.description: Whether something was sent for it.

oneOf.description:
The body did not return a value the Effect journal keeps after
something was sent, and the Effect is not repeatable: it never runs
again until a person reconciles it, and every later declaration of
its key raises `effect_uncertain`. The SDK raises `effect_uncertain`
with the body's error as its cause, or propagates a cut-short
body's error unchanged.

cause.description:
The Error code the body's value met, `effect_output_invalid`,
when it returned one the Effect journal does not keep.

effect.description: The Effect left uncertain, as the Run report lists it.

EffectOpenParams.description:
What `effect.open` takes: the Run, the Effect key and whether its body
is safe to run again.

attempt.description:
The crawl attempt whose handler's `ctx.run` declares the Effect
(ADR 0093), whose crawl request is the key's namespace. Absent, the
key's namespace is the Run.

key.description:
The Effect key, chosen by the program: 1 to 255 Unicode code
points. Its namespace is the crawl request in a handler and the Run
elsewhere.

repeatable.description:
Whether the body is safe to run again: a body that sent something
and did not return then runs again at its next declaration instead
of leaving its Effect uncertain. `false` by default.

run_id.description: The Run whose Effect journal keeps the Effect.

oneOf.description:
The Effect journal holds no answer: run the body, then
`effect.close` the entry.

entry.description: The Effect journal entry, which `effect.close` names.

idempotency_key.description:
An opaque key, the same on every attempt and resume of this
Effect on any machine and different in every Run and install,
for the body to send as a site's `Idempotency-Key`.

oneOf.description:
An earlier attempt or start performed the Effect: the body does not
run, and the output it returned then is the answer.

output.description: What the body returned, or absent when it returned nothing.

oneOf.description:
A person answered "it happened" (ADR 0029): the body does not run,
and no output is known.
It returned a value, or nothing.

output.description:
What it returned: JSON up to `effect.output.max_size` bytes, or
absent when it returned nothing.

oneOf.description:
It raised an error, which the SDK propagates, or wraps in
`effect_uncertain` when the Effect is left uncertain.

It was cut short: a cancellation or its attempt's end, whose error
the SDK propagates unchanged (ADRs 0080 and 0093).

Email.description: An e-mail address the page shows.

text.description:

EndingError.description: An Error code a Run's ending raises, with its message and details.

product.description: The Product the engine runs as.

product_major.description: The major of its Product version, which names its per-major state.

protocol_version.description: The protocol version the engine speaks.

EngineStep.description: The engine's step that raised a Human pause.

oneOf.description: A login recovery (ADR 0006).
The Challenge ladder (ADR 0035).

EvaluateParams.description:
What `page.evaluate` takes: the page, the function's source, its

arg.description: Its one argument, JSON; absent for none.

function.description:
The page function's JavaScript source: a function, called with
`arg`, or an expression, which takes none.

world.description: Where it runs; the main world when absent.

Evaluated.description:
What `page.evaluate` answers: the function's result, awaited when it is
a promise.

value.description: The result as JSON; absent when it was `undefined`.

after.description:
The last event the Client read, `{engine_instance, position}`: the
subscription resumes after it, or starts with `events.resync` when
the engine no longer holds it or another engine instance gave it, as
after a Daemon restart. Absent, it starts with the next event.

system_info.description:
Whether it also takes `engine.system_info`, the Resource governor's
periodic readings; false by default, so a subscription that reads
only what changes sees no periodic event.

ExplainedSetting.description: One setting as `config explain` shows it.

applied.description:
Whether this engine applies it: `false` for a key only the other
Product honours, which a shared file may hold (ADR 0087).

cap.description: An Operator policy's cap on it, if any.

fixed_for_run.description:
Whether it is fixed for a Run's life: a resume that changes it is
refused with `setting_not_applicable`, and only a new Run takes
another value (ADRs 0102 and 0120).

locked_by.description:
The layer that locked it, if any: an Operator policy's lock, a
Recipe that declares it without exposing it, or the default for an
honesty guarantee.

origin.description: For the run layer, where the value came from.

preset.description:
When a level's preset gave the value, at `layer`, that level, which
`config explain` shows as "preset of `run_state.durability: full`"
in place of the layer (ADR 0142).

products.description: The Products that honour it, from its Product mark (ADR 0095).

user_settable.description:
Whether user configuration may set it: its authority lets user
configuration hold it and no lower layer locked it, so a person
surface may offer its user-level value for editing (ADR 0031).

value.description:
The effective value, or for a key this engine does not apply, the
value its highest layer wrote.

weakens.description:
Whether its value weakens a guarantee class or switches off a costly
control, which the results it touches are marked with (ADR 0028).

yields_to.description:
The setting its value yields to, with that setting's value and
layer, when one that is set keeps its value from taking effect:
`fetch.http_from` away from `browser` yields to the Run's
`session.source`, whose Sessions hold a login and so send their HTTP

ExportedAuditEntry.description:
One entry of an exported Audit log, one line of its JSONL: the entry
and the hash that chains it to the line before it.

chained.description:
Whether its hash chains it to the entry before it: `false` for an
entry of a Run whose `security.audit_chain` was off, whose hash is
`SHA-256` of 32 zero bytes and its own canonical JSON alone, and
which `audit verify` steps over while it verifies the chain around
it; left out when chained.

details.description:
What its kind records, such as a Secret reference and the domain it
was sent to, never a secret's value.

hash.description:
`SHA-256(previous hash ‖ RFC 8785 canonical JSON of the entry)`, in
lowercase hex; an anchor's is the last pruned entry's.

kind.description: Its kind, a value of the shared type `audit_kind`.

layer.description:
The settings layer its event came from, such as an Operator policy
that switched a control off; none where no layer applies.

run_id.description: The Run it happened in; none outside a Run.

sequence.description: Its place in the chain, from 1.

surface.description:
The surface the actor acted through, such as `kennel` for a person
in the Kennel; none for the engine's own events.

FieldLocator.description:
What finds a field's element, named by `kind`: a CSS selector or an
`XPath` expression, each read alike on every tier, a page a fetch tier
serves from its document reading it as a browser reads it.

oneOf.description: A CSS selector.

An `XPath` 1.0 expression that finds nodes, with no namespace
prefix and no variable; a value field reads the first node it finds
in document order, when that node is an element, and a list every
element it finds. Under a row's element it is evaluated with that
element as its context node.

FieldMatch.description:
The `match` before a field's transform (ADR 0123): a capture group of a
regular expression, in the `regex` crate's syntax (ADR 0081), over the
text read; that group's text is what the transform reads.

group.description: The capture group, 1 by default; 0 is the whole match.

FieldTransform.description:
A field's Value transform (ADR 0123), named by `kind`, each
locale-dependent one stating its locale, a BCP 47 tag. A `number`,
`date` or `date_time` reads the machine-readable value of a `<time
datetime>`, a `<data value>` or an element's `content` attribute in its
invariant form (ISO 8601, a plain decimal with a dot), whatever the
locale; a text printed for people is read under its locale's CLDR
forms: a number in its digits, separators and grouping, a date or a
date and time in one of its short, medium or long forms with a
four-digit year; any other text is not a value.

oneOf.description: The text read: a string.

An integer or decimal: a JSON number, never through a float, so a
decimal a JSON number cannot hold exactly is not a value.
A date: `YYYY-MM-DD`.

A date and time: RFC 3339 with its offset, the one the text states,
else `time_zone`'s at that time; one stating neither is not a value.

time_zone.description: The time zone, an IANA name, of a text that states none.

FillParams.description:
What `locator.fill` takes: the locator whose field it fills, and the
text.

value.description: The text the field holds afterwards; an empty text clears it.

FormatsParams.description: What `page.formats` takes: the page, and the formats it asks for.

one value, which a Record can carry and a Dataset's schema can be
generated from (ADR 0103). A format left out is left out of the result.

contacts.description:
The e-mail addresses, telephone numbers and social profiles the
page shows.

html.description: The page's HTML: its main content by default.

images.description: The page's images, each with its URL resolved and its `alt`.

links.description: The page's links, each with its URL resolved.

markdown.description: The page's content as Markdown, with GFM's tables.

media.description: The page's video and audio sources, each with its URL resolved.

metadata.description:
The page's metadata: its title, description, canonical URL,
language, Open Graph and Twitter tags, JSON-LD blocks and microdata
items.

tables.description: The page's tables, as rows of cells.

text.description: The text of the page's main content, a paragraph per block.

GotoParams.description:
What `page.goto` takes: the page, the URL it goes to, and when it
answers.

timeout.description:
How long the navigation may take, in milliseconds, at least 1:
absent for `timeout.navigation`, `null` for none, though an

wait_until.description: When the navigation answers; `load` when absent.

before the Clean-up rules: what `content()` returns there.

The main content the extractor finds, the default.

raised_by.description: Whether the program or the engine raised it.

reason.description: Why, as the program or the engine said it.

until.description: The condition that ends it by itself, as text.

alt.description:

src.description: Its `src` as the document writes it.

url.description:

It was migrated: checkpointed and stopped, to be resumed from its

The resource governor ran out of a resource for it, and it stopped

folder.description: For storage, the folder whose filesystem filled.

Who stopped a Run as an abort, the `by` of its `abort` stop reason; a

oneOf.description: A Client, through `run.abort`.
The program, such as through `run.stop` (ADR 0102).
The browser, outside every Client.

StorageLevel.description: A filesystem's storage level (ADR 0122), from the best to the worst.

Its free space or inodes fell below `storage.low_free`: the Runs
writing to it shed what they can do without and carry
`storage_low`.

Its free space or inodes fell below `storage.critical_free`: every

What `events.subscribe` answers when its subscription ends without the

SystemInfo.description:
What the governor read and decided at one sample: the payload of
`engine.system_info`.

last_resort.description:
Whether memory stayed critical at the floor past
`governor.last_resort_after`.

pressure_source.description: The reading that holds it above `normal`; none at `normal`.

Table.description:
A table of the page, in document order, a table inside another listed
on its own: each row its cells' text, white space collapsed, a row's
header kept as its first cell.

caption.description: Its `<caption>`'s text; `null` when it has none.

header_rows.description:
Its header rows: its `<thead>`'s, else the rows it begins with whose
cells are all `<th>`.

Tag.description: An opaque text a Run is tagged with (ADR 0036).

Tags.description: A Run's tags, in the order given.

TimeRange.description:
A span of time: from its first point, included, until its last,
excluded; an end left out leaves that side open.

until.description: The point it ends before, excluded.

UncertainEffect.description: An Effect a Run left uncertain (ADR 0106), until a person reconciles it.

crawl_request.description: The crawl request it ran for, in a crawl.

first_command.description: The first command sent for it.

instruction.description: Its instruction, for an AI action.

key.description: Its key, for a declared Effect.

UnreadField.description:
A field its page did not give, so its value is null (ADRs 0079 and
0123).

field.description:
The field, a JSON Pointer into the values read: `/price`, or
`/offers/1/price` for a row's.

text.description:
The text read, where one was: the text its `match` did not match, or
that its transform does not read as a value.

oneOf.description: Its locator found no element.
Its element has no such attribute.
Its `match` did not match the text, or its group took no part.
Its transform does not read the text as a value.
A `date_time` whose text states no offset, with no `time_zone`.

Unready.description:
Why a Daemon cannot take a new Run now, as its ops listener's
`/readyz` and `daemon health` check it (ADR 0050).

oneOf.description: It drains, taking no Run (ADR 0049).
Its run state cannot be written.
A browser its configuration uses is not installed.

Its Resource governor is at its last resort: memory stayed critical
at the floor past `governor.last_resort_after` (ADR 0040).

The filesystem holding its run state, or the Goodfetch home's, is
at the `critical` storage level, where a new Run's start is refused
(ADR 0122).

UrlMatcher.description:
A URL pattern the engine matches (ADR 0081): a glob as Playwright reads
one, or a regular expression in the `regex` crate's syntax. A predicate
runs in the program, which routes every URL and falls back for the
requests it does not match.

oneOf.description: A glob, such as `**/*.png`.
A regular expression, matched anywhere in the URL.

UsageAmount.description: An amount of a Usage kind counted in a currency, or as a count.

amount.description: A count, or millionths of the currency.

currency.description: The currency, an ISO 4217 code; none for a count.

limits.description: Every Limit of the Usage ledger, by scope, with its Usage.

UsageRaiseParams.description:
What `usage.raise` takes: a Limit a person sets, which replaces every
Limit of its scope, Usage kind, currency and period that is not a
managed Operator policy's, keeping the Usage counted against them.

amount.description:
How much it allows per period from now on: a count of the Usage
kind, or millionths of the currency.

currency.description: The currency it caps the price in, an ISO 4217 code.

period.description: The period it counts over; none for a Limit that never starts again.

scope_id.description:
Which one of its kind; the person's own when absent (their Client
connection, their person, the engine's Daemon, the install).

UsageSetParams.description:
What `usage.set` takes: a Limit of the caller's own, which holds beside
the others, so the tightest one holds.

amount.description:
How much it allows per period: a count of the Usage kind, or
millionths of the currency.

currency.description: The currency it caps the price in, an ISO 4217 code.

period.description: The period it counts over; none for a Limit that never starts again.

scope_id.description:
Which one of its kind; the caller's own when absent (its Client
connection, its person, the engine's Daemon, the install).

value.description: Its new value; `null` removes it from user configuration.

diff.description: Each key the write changed, with its values before and after.

changes.description: The changes, made in order, in one write.

ValueField.description:
A value field (ADRs 0123 and 0147): the first element its locator
ladder finds in the page, its locator tried first, then each of its
`fallbacks` in turn until one finds an element; its text, its runs of
white space read as one space and trimmed, or one of its attributes, an
`href` or `src` resolved against the document's base URL; optionally a
capture group of a regular expression over that text; then its Value
transform. A field the page does not give is null, with why.

attribute.description: The attribute read in place of the element's text.

fallbacks.description:
Its locator ladder's further rungs: when `locator` finds no
element, the first of these, in order, that finds one supplies it;
in a list, the first that finds any; in rows, the first that finds
one under the row's element. Each is checked as `locator` is when
the call or crawl starts.

match.description: The `match` that picks the text its transform reads.

Verdict.description: Whether a Run's own checks prove what it committed (ADR 0029).

oneOf.description:
Every check the Run relies on passed, none was switched off, and no
Effect is left uncertain.
A declared Success check failed.
Everything else: a person reviews it.

WaitForCountParams.description:
What `locator.wait_for_count` takes: the locator and the count its
matches must reach.

timeout.description:
How long the wait may take, in milliseconds, at least 1: absent for
`timeout.wait`, `null` for none, though an enclosing timeout still
applies (ADR 0080).

WaitForExchangeParams.description:
What `page.wait_for_request` and `page.wait_for_response` take: the
page, and the URLs of the requests they wait for; any request when none
is given.

timeout.description:
How long the wait may take, in milliseconds, at least 1: absent for
`timeout.wait`, `null` for none, though an enclosing timeout still
applies (ADR 0080).

WaitForFunctionParams.description:
What `page.wait_for_function` takes: the page, the function's source,
its argument, its world, and how often it is checked.

arg.description: Its one argument, JSON; absent for none.

function.description:
The page function's JavaScript source: a function, called with
`arg`, or an expression, which takes none.

polling_interval.description:
The milliseconds between two checks, at least 1; absent, about one
frame's, 16.

timeout.description:
How long the wait may take, in milliseconds, at least 1: absent for
`timeout.wait`, `null` for none, though an enclosing timeout still
applies (ADR 0080).

world.description: Where it runs; the main world when absent.

WaitForLoadStateParams.description: What `page.wait_for_load_state` takes: the page and the state.

timeout.description:
How long the wait may take, in milliseconds, at least 1: absent for
`timeout.wait`, `null` for none, though an enclosing timeout still
applies (ADR 0080).

WaitForRequestFinishedParams.description:
What `page.wait_for_request_finished` takes: the page, and the URLs of
the requests it waits for; any request when none is given.

timeout.description:
How long the wait may take, in milliseconds, at least 1: absent for
`timeout.wait`, `null` for none, though an enclosing timeout still
applies (ADR 0080).

WaitForUrlParams.description:
What `page.wait_for_url` takes: the page, the URL it waits for, and the
state a new document must reach.

timeout.description:
How long the wait may take, in milliseconds, at least 1: absent for
`timeout.wait`, `null` for none, though an enclosing timeout still
applies (ADR 0080).

wait_until.description:
The state a new document at that URL must reach; `load` when
absent. A change within the document waits for none.

WaitUntil.description:
When a navigation answers, by the state its document reached
(Playwright's `waitUntil`).

oneOf.description:
Once the browser committed the document, its response received: a
body cut after that is left to the body's read.
Once the document fired `DOMContentLoaded`.
Once the document fired `load`.

added.description:
Whether it was added: false when the Operator policy denied it
already, which then changed nothing and recorded nothing.

domain.description: The domain, as `wall.denied_domains` now lists it.

reason.description: The reason, as the Audit log records it.

WeakenedSetting.description:
A setting that weakened a safeguard for a Run (ADR 0028): its key, its
value, the layer that set it and, for the run layer, where the value came
from.

origin.description: For the run layer, where the value came from.

preset.description:
When a level's preset gave the value, at `layer`, that level, such
as `run_state.durability: off` (ADR 0142).

WebError.description:
What `page.page_error` reports, `WebError`: an exception the page did
not catch (ADR 0085), never a `PageError`, ADR 0079's group.

name.description:
Its name, such as `TypeError`; `Error` for a thrown value that is no
error.

stack.description: Its stack as the browser renders it, when it has one.

WebSocketClosed.description: What `web_socket.close` reports: a page's WebSocket closed.

WebSocketFrame.description:
What `web_socket.frame_sent` and `web_socket.frame_received` report: one
message frame of a page's WebSocket.

binary.description: Whether it is a binary frame.

payload.description: Its payload: its text, or for a binary frame its bytes in Base64.

oneOf.description:
The page's own world, where its globals are, as Playwright's and
Puppeteer's default: the Session's Provenance marks the call.

A world of the engine's own in the page's document, which shares
its DOM but neither sees nor is seen by the page's scripts.

error_codes.description: The host has addresses only in an IP family the Session holds no local address of, such as IPv6 addresses for a Session bound to an IPv4 address. Add a local address of that family to the run's local addresses, or reach the host another way.
error_codes.name: address_family_unavailable

error_codes.description: A pinned download the call needed failed: the network, an HTTP status, or bytes whose digest is not the pinned one. Retry, or install beforehand with the Product's `browser install`, or point `GOODFETCH_BROWSERS_PATH` at a prepared cache.
error_codes.name: artifact_download_failed

error_codes.description: The `offline` setting refused a pinned download the call needed. Run the Product's `browser install` beforehand where the cache is writable, point `GOODFETCH_BROWSERS_PATH` at a prepared cache, or lift `offline` where it was set.
error_codes.name: artifact_unavailable_offline

error_codes.description: The site refused the document a navigation reached with a Block cause the engine cannot get past, such as a rate limit, an IP block or a challenge: raised by the call that waited for that navigation, or else by the page's next call. The Session stays open with its cookies, never replaced, and nothing waits on the site's `Retry-After`: the program decides whether to wait, open another Session or pause for a person. The details name the cause, the URL, the status and `retry_after`, the time the site asked for or `null`.
error_codes.name: blocked

error_codes.description: The Run's folder holds no body of this ID: the Run or the body is unknown, or the ID is not a body's.
error_codes.name: body_not_found

error_codes.description: The browser no longer holds the response's body, as after the page navigated away or once its buffer evicted it, or the response has none, as a redirect's: the engine keeps a body only for a response obtained through `page.wait_for_request_finished`, `route.fetch` or `page.request`, which the fix names. Where Playwright and Puppeteer say "Request content was evicted from inspector cache". A retry finds the body gone all the same.
error_codes.name: body_unavailable

error_codes.description: The Browser host the engine reached is of a version this engine cannot drive. Upgrade the Browser host, which either Product's executable runs as its `browser-host` command.
error_codes.name: browser_host_outdated

error_codes.description: The link to the hosted Browser host that runs the Session's browser is lost: the call fails, as does each later call until the link returns, and the Session stays open; while the Session is opening, the lost link is the open's failure. A person's own Browser host never raises it: its Session goes offline and the Run waits in a Human pause until the host is back.
error_codes.name: browser_host_unreachable

error_codes.description: The browser's build is installed, but it did not start or did not open the page: it exited, or its connection refused or fell silent. The details name its executable and how it ended.
error_codes.name: browser_launch_failed

error_codes.description: The Session would launch the full Chrome for Testing build headless on macOS from a process with no GUI session, such as a `LaunchAgent` in the Background session or an SSH login, where that build cannot start. Nothing was launched. Set `browser.headless_shell: true` to launch the headless shell, or run the engine in a login session.
error_codes.name: browser_needs_gui_session

error_codes.description: The browser build a launch needs is not in the Browser cache and the engine cannot write that cache, such as an image's read-only `GOODFETCH_BROWSERS_PATH`; or a browser named by channel or path is not there. Run the Product's `browser install` where the cache is writable, install the browser of that channel, or correct the path.
error_codes.name: browser_not_installed

error_codes.description: Chromium's sandbox cannot start on this host, so the engine launches no browser. `environment` names what refuses it (Docker's or containerd's default seccomp profile, Kubernetes' `RuntimeDefault`, Ubuntu's AppArmor restriction on unprivileged user namespaces, or `unknown` for a refusal the probe does not recognise, which the message names), and `fix` the fix; an Operator policy may instead switch `security.browser_sandbox` off, which the run reports.
error_codes.name: browser_sandbox_unavailable

error_codes.description: The call was stopped in flight, at its next cancellation point: its Client sent `$/cancel`, or what it needed was closed under it.
error_codes.name: call_cancelled

error_codes.description: A capability this engine cannot provide where a setting asks for it, such as a Session opening from a Session source of a kind this engine does not read: the details name the setting, the layer that set it and what it asked for, and its fix names the value that does without it.
error_codes.name: capability_unavailable

error_codes.description: A `cdp_url` Session source names an address ADR 0056's rules refuse, before any connection: a private address from a value that is not Operator-configured, loopback from a Client acting for a model (its project configuration included) or a Recipe, or a private address under `egress.no_private_endpoints`. The details name the address without its query or credentials, the settings layer that gave it, the rule, the address it resolved to and the fix: set the address in Operator policy or in user configuration, or give a public address.
error_codes.name: cdp_url_not_allowed

error_codes.description: Something answered at a `cdp_url` Session source's address, but no browser speaks CDP there: an HTTP status and content type, a WebSocket that refused the upgrade, a CDP target that is not a browser (`page`, `node`, `worker`), or a product the engine does not drive, which `observed` says. The details name the address without its query or credentials, the settings layer that gave it and the fix: give the browser's endpoint, `http://host:port` or `ws://…/devtools/browser/<id>`, and when the same host serves `/json/version`, the browser address found there, which `browser_url` holds.
error_codes.name: cdp_url_not_browser

error_codes.description: A `cdp_url` Session source's address answered 401 or 403 to the HTTP request or the WebSocket upgrade. The details name the address without its query or credentials, the settings layer that gave it, the status, each header name sent with its Secret reference, never its value, and the fix: check the Secret references in `headers`.
error_codes.name: cdp_url_unauthorized

error_codes.description: Nothing answered at a `cdp_url` Session source's address when the call that opens the Session connected to it: its name did not resolve, the connection was refused or reset, or TLS failed. It fails at once, never waiting for the address. The details name the address without its query or credentials, the settings layer that gave it, the failure and the fix: start the browser with remote debugging on that port, or correct the address.
error_codes.name: cdp_url_unreachable

error_codes.description: A pinned host presented a certificate whose public key is not its pin, or its pin row cannot be read, so nothing was sent to it, nor is for the rest of the run. The details carry the host, both SHA-256 hashes and the fix: a person accepts the new key with `certs accept` in an interactive prompt, which no agent, Recipe or `--json` command can do.
error_codes.name: certificate_changed

error_codes.description: A host's certificate failed verification and no exception covers its domain, so nothing was sent to it. The details name the host, the failure (`expired`, `not_yet_valid`, `unknown_issuer`, `name_mismatch`, `self_signed`, `revoked`, or another failure as text) and, in `fix`, the setting that makes an exception for that domain.
error_codes.name: certificate_invalid

error_codes.description: The page met a Challenge that every step of the ladder ended without passing: a timed wait for an invisible challenge, the Challenge solver when `challenge.solve` is on, and a Human pause when a person can answer and `session.recovery.human_pause` is on. Only the Page check declares a Challenge passed. The Session stays open with its cookies; an Agent's page gets it as its action's outcome. The details name the Block cause, `challenge` or `captcha`, the URL, the status and `steps`, each step tried with why it ended.
error_codes.name: challenge_unsolved

error_codes.description: The call was made on a value its program had closed: a Connection, or a Run, Session or Page under it. A value never reopens: connect again, or start the Run again by its Run ID.
error_codes.name: closed

error_codes.description: The host cannot confine the Plugin as it must run: it has no seccomp at all (WSL1), or neither user namespaces nor Landlock ABI 6 (a container under Docker's default seccomp profile on a kernel before 6.12), or it cannot provide the network level the Plugin's manifest declares, which is never silently weakened. A third-party Plugin is always refused; a first-party one, shipped in the engine's own release, too, unless the Operator policy's `plugins.<name>.reduced_confinement` lets it run with the confinement the host offers. A Bridge Sink is refused with it under a container runtime that runs as root.
error_codes.name: confinement_unavailable

error_codes.description: The call was made in another process than the one that opened its Connection, such as a child created by `fork`: a Connection and every Run, Session or Page under it belong to the process that opened them. Connect in the child process.
error_codes.name: connection_forked

error_codes.description: The Connection to the engine dropped before the call was answered, so whether it took effect is unknown. The Client connects again by itself; make the call again once it has, after checking that an Effect did not happen.
error_codes.name: connection_lost

error_codes.description: The Connection already holds as many calls waiting for their answer, or as many bytes waiting to be written to the engine, as its bounds allow, so the call was refused at once and never sent; the calls made before it go on. The details name the bound, `pending_calls` or `queued_write_bytes`, and its value. Wait for earlier calls to end, or raise `connection.max_pending_calls` or `connection.max_queued_write_bytes` in `connect()`'s `settings`.
error_codes.name: connection_overloaded

error_codes.description: The foreground Daemon is draining on `SIGTERM`: it takes no run and checkpoints every live run as resumable, then exits. Start or resume the run on the Daemon that replaces it.
error_codes.name: daemon_draining

error_codes.description: No Daemon could be reached, so nothing was called: nothing answers where `GOODFETCH_URL` or its runtime file says it listens, it closed the Connection before it answered `hello`, as one does for a wrong `GOODFETCH_TOKEN`, it went away while the command connected, or its files cannot be read or its major's pick cannot be started. The message says which, and the `fix` what to do.
error_codes.name: daemon_unreachable

error_codes.description: The call's deadline passed before what it waited for came, such as a response's first byte or a navigation. Its `limit` names the timeout's setting, its value and the layer that set it: raise that setting, or wait for the right thing.
error_codes.name: deadline_exceeded

error_codes.description: The dialog was answered already, by an earlier `accept` or `dismiss`, or it closed, its handler having ended or the dialog having got its default: the first answer stands and this one changed nothing.
error_codes.name: dialog_already_handled

error_codes.description: The program runs on an edge runtime, Cloudflare Workers, Vercel's edge runtime or Deno Deploy, which ends what it runs with its request, and asked for code the engine would call after it: a crawl's handlers, an SDK handler, a Hook in code or a lent page. Nothing was sent. Run that code as a Recipe on the Daemon, and start or poll its Run from the edge function.
error_codes.name: edge_handlers_unsupported

error_codes.description: An Effect key is empty or longer than 255 Unicode code points (ADR 0106). The details name the key.
error_codes.name: effect_key_invalid

error_codes.description: An Effect key was declared again in one attempt while its body runs, or after this attempt got its answer (ADR 0106): a loop that left its varying part out of the key would otherwise perform one Effect for many. Put what varies in the key. The details name the key.
error_codes.name: effect_key_reused

error_codes.description: An Effect's body returned a value that is not JSON or is larger than `effect.output.max_size`, when nothing was sent for it (ADR 0106); the entry is dropped. After a send it is the cause of `effect_uncertain`. The details name the key, the value's size and the limit.
error_codes.name: effect_output_invalid

error_codes.description: An Effect may or may not have happened (ADRs 0091 and 0106): its body sent something and did not return a value the Effect journal keeps, so the engine never runs it again until a person reconciles it ("it happened", "it did not happen" or "leave uncertain"). The details name the Effect journal `entry`, the `key`, the `crawl_request`, the `reason` (`failed_after_send`, `interrupted` or `journal_incomplete`), the `first_command` sent and `since` when.
error_codes.name: effect_uncertain

error_codes.description: The run's egress policy refused a request before it connected: a host the domain policy does not allow, an address that is not globally reachable, or a scheme no request may use. The details name the URL, the rule, the address when there is one and the setting that would allow it.
error_codes.name: egress_refused

error_codes.description: The engine ended before its Connection was closed, so the call has no answer. An Attached engine's details carry its exit code or signal and the last 64 KiB of its stderr; a linked engine's carry none.
error_codes.name: engine_exited

error_codes.description: `connect()` found no engine executable to start: the Product's engine-path variable names no executable, or the Product's platform package is not installed. The `fix` names the variable or the package.
error_codes.name: engine_not_found

error_codes.description: The engine wrote a line that is not one JSON-RPC message on the Connection, such as a log line on an Attached engine's stdout, so the Client ended the Connection. A bug in Goodfetch: report it with the line its details carry.
error_codes.name: engine_output_invalid

error_codes.description: A bug in Goodfetch made the engine panic, which ended what `ended` names and only that: for `call`, this call, while its Connection, its Run and its Page go on. Making the same call again is likely to hit the same bug. Report it with the crash report `crash_report` names, a file in the engine's crash-report folder on its machine.
error_codes.name: engine_panicked

error_codes.description: Windows refused to start the file: Smart App Control, or another App Control policy, blocks executables without a signature or reputation it trusts. Goodfetch never re-signs a file it did not build. For a browser, use the Goodfetch Chromium or an installed Chrome by channel; otherwise turn Smart App Control off, or ask the device's administrator to allow the file.
error_codes.name: executable_blocked_by_smart_app_control

error_codes.description: The bytes of a file could not be written: no space or quota left, or an I/O error, or any failure where the engine keeps its files. No partial file is left. Free space where the files go, or ask the Daemon's operator, then make the same call again.
error_codes.name: file_write_failed

error_codes.description: A file, such as a run state or a Checkpoint, is of a format version this engine cannot read: a newer minor or major, written by a newer engine, which `fix` says to upgrade to, or an older major, which `upgrade-files` upgrades. The file is left as it is.
error_codes.name: format_version_unsupported

error_codes.description: A header value the engine would send holds a CR, an LF or a NUL, which could end the header and start another, so it is refused before it reaches the wire or the browser. The details name the header and the character, never the value. Remove the character from the value.
error_codes.name: header_value_invalid

error_codes.description: A Hook raised, so its work failed: an attempt commits nothing, and one that failed at the Record stage commits none of what it staged. The message always names the exception. The details name the stage, the Hook, the request's Label (`null` at a lifecycle stage or outside a crawl), the exception's type, message and stack, and the Goodfetch code raised inside (`null` for the program's own exception). A wrapped code is retried when its own retryable flag says so; in a crawl, the program's own exception only when `crawl.retry.handler_failed` is on, since a bug fails the same way every time, and either retry draws on `crawl.retry.max`.
error_codes.name: hook_failed

error_codes.description: A bug in Goodfetch: an object such as a Session or a page received an event its state cannot receive. Report it with the object, the state and the event its details carry.
error_codes.name: internal

error_codes.description: A newer engine wrote a Limit this engine cannot evaluate, and it may cover the run; the details name it. Upgrade the engine.
error_codes.name: limit_not_understood

error_codes.description: A start that names an existing Run gave a Limit above the Run's Limit as it stands; the details name its Usage kind, its currency, the amount given and the one standing. A program only lowers a Limit: ask a person to raise it.
error_codes.name: limit_raise_refused

error_codes.description: A Limit that covers the run has nothing left in its period; the details name its scope, its Usage kind, its period and when it starts again. Wait for the next period, or ask a person to raise it.
error_codes.name: limit_reached

error_codes.description: A listener the program registered with `on` on a value whose events the engine publishes on its event stream, such as a Session's, held more events than its queue takes, the bound set where the Connection opens, 1,024 by default, so the SDK removed it once it got the events it held. Only that listener loses events: the Connection's Subscription and its other listeners go on. Its details name the event and how many events the listener lost: make the listener return sooner, or raise the bound, and listen again.
error_codes.name: listener_events_lost

error_codes.description: A listener the program registered with `on` threw, or its awaitable failed, so the SDK removed it. Raised once, by the next call on the value it listened to, which is not sent and leaves the value open, or by the `close()` that closes that value, its own or one above it, after closing it; when the value is released first, the SDK logs it at error instead. Its details name the event, and its cause is the listener's exception: fix the listener and listen again.
error_codes.name: listener_failed

error_codes.description: `egress.local_addresses` yields no address this host can send from: a listed address the host does not hold, an interface it does not have or that holds no address, or an IPv6 prefix with none of the host's addresses in it and, on Linux, not routed locally with `net.ipv6.ip_nonlocal_bind` on; or a Session whose browser this engine does not launch on this machine (a Borrowed browser, a third-party CDP browser, a Browser host's) or whose `https://` proxy the egress relay does not chain through. The binding is never ignored: assign the address, correct the value, route the prefix to the host, or open the Session on a browser the engine launches here.
error_codes.name: local_address_unavailable

error_codes.description: The document the navigation reached is a login page, even one answered with a 200: the Session's login is lost, judged by its Page check's `login_page`, or by the built-in detector when it declares none. The page stays on the login page, the Session open with its cookies. The details name the URL, the status and what judged it.
error_codes.name: logged_out

error_codes.description: The engine's own resolver got no usable answer for the host name: its name servers timed out, refused the query, failed or could not be reached. Check the name servers of the system's resolver configuration, or map the name with the `resolve` setting.
error_codes.name: name_lookup_failed

error_codes.description: The resolver found no address for the host name. The engine's own resolver, used on Linux and for Sessions with a local address, reads the system's resolver configuration and hosts file but asks neither NSS modules (such as a directory service or a VPN client's) nor multicast DNS, so a name only they resolve, such as a `.local` name, fails here. Map such a name to its address with the `resolve` setting, or correct the name.
error_codes.name: name_not_resolved

error_codes.description: The navigation reached no document: the browser's network error, such as `net::ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED`, is in the details, or the browser failed it for a reason it did not name.
error_codes.name: navigation_failed

error_codes.description: Another navigation of the page started before this one committed, so this one reached no document: the page went where the other took it.
error_codes.name: navigation_interrupted

error_codes.description: The call asks a Daemon about itself, and this engine is an Attached engine. Ask the Daemon of the major, found through its runtime file, or run `daemon status`.
error_codes.name: not_a_daemon

error_codes.description: The running engine's Product does not carry what was asked: a Client that needs Foxhound reached a Collie engine, or a call, a setting or a value only Foxhound carries reached one. Run it with Foxhound, which contains everything Collie does, or connect to a Foxhound engine.
error_codes.name: not_in_product

error_codes.description: The program asked AI work for its output only if verified, and its Verdict is not `verified`, so no output is returned. The details hold the Verdict, the reasons it is not `verified` and the model's claim, which is never proof; the result itself still holds how the work ended.
error_codes.name: not_verified

error_codes.description: The document the navigation reached is neither the expected page nor the login page of its Session's Page check, `session.page_check`, whatever its HTTP status: a page the program did not mean to reach, such as an error page or a layout the site changed. The page stays on that document. The details name its URL and status.
error_codes.name: page_check_failed

error_codes.description: The page's renderer crashed, or its browser process was lost while the call ran; `browser_exit` says how the browser ended when it is what was lost. The page is gone: open another.
error_codes.name: page_crashed

error_codes.description: Some of a page's events are lost. Either the engine fell too far behind the browser's events of a page that is still open and stopped reading them: the page's `page.on` listeners, waits and `response.body` reads raise this rather than answer from missing events, and the Run trace records it, while the page's other calls still work; open another page to follow its events. Or one `page.on` call's Client took too few of its events, granting too few credits, so 1,024 waited unsent: that call raises this once it sent them; listen again and grant credits as events are read.
error_codes.name: page_events_lost

error_codes.description: A page function threw in the page, or did not parse, or is an expression given an argument, which only a function takes. The details give the error's name, its message and the page's stack. A page function sees only the page and its one argument, never the program's variables, so a `ReferenceError`'s fix names the argument: pass the value in it.
error_codes.name: page_function_failed

error_codes.description: A handler the program gave a page failed, such as a route's handler that threw: its request was aborted unless it was answered already, never sent half-changed, and its route was removed; a dialog handler's dialog got its default and the handler was removed. Raised by the call that waited on that request, such as the `goto` whose document it was, or by the call the dialog blocked, or else by the next call on its page. The details name the handler, the URL of the request or of the dialog's document, and what the failure said.
error_codes.name: page_handler_failed

error_codes.description: Memory was critical and the page held more than `governor.browser.page_memory_cap`, so the Resource governor ended it once no call on it was in flight. The page is gone: open another and try again, which the governor admits once memory frees up.
error_codes.name: page_memory_exceeded

error_codes.description: A page function's result, or its argument, holds a value outside JSON, such as a DOM node, `NaN`, `Infinity`, a function, a `Map`, a `BigInt` or a cycle, which Playwright would have turned into `undefined`, silently. The details name the first such value's path from `$`, its kind and the fix: return the JSON the program needs, such as an element's text or attribute instead of the element.
error_codes.name: page_value_invalid

error_codes.description: The path the program chose cannot be written for a reason the path causes: permission denied, a read-only filesystem, a folder at the path, a file where a parent folder should be, a name the filesystem refuses, a file too large for that filesystem, or a path not found once its parents are made. No partial file is left. Change the path.
error_codes.name: path_not_writable

error_codes.description: A name or path from outside input would leave the folder the engine writes it in, or is no safe file name on Linux, macOS or Windows: a `..` or `.` part, an absolute, drive, UNC, verbatim or device path, a name Windows reserves for a device, an alternate data stream, a character Windows forbids or a control character, a trailing dot or space, a part longer than 255 bytes, an empty part or a name that is not in Unicode's composed form. It is refused on every OS alike. The details name it and its hazard.
error_codes.name: path_unsafe

error_codes.description: A URL pattern the engine cannot match: a regular expression with look-around, a back-reference or another construct outside the `regex` crate's syntax, or a glob with nested or unmatched braces. The details name the construct; match the URL with a predicate instead, which runs in the program.
error_codes.name: pattern_unsupported

error_codes.description: Only a person gives this answer: no agent surface, SDK, script or command run under `--json` or without a terminal may. Run the Operation's command in a terminal, where the CLI has one, or answer it in the Kennel where the Kennel offers the Operation.
error_codes.name: person_required

error_codes.description: The process Plugin crashed while it held the call, and restarts with backoff. A read or an idempotent write fails with it and is retried under its lease; an Effect with no check is never retried blindly, but reported uncertain for Reconciliation instead. Repeated crashes quarantine the Plugin.
error_codes.name: plugin_crashed

error_codes.description: The Operator policy's digest changed since it was read, as by a hand edit, so nothing was written; `fix` says to read it again.
error_codes.name: policy_conflict

error_codes.description: The engine does not speak the protocol version the Client's `hello` names: it accepts its own major with the same or an older minor. Upgrade the older side.
error_codes.name: protocol_version_unsupported

error_codes.description: The Session's proxy answered `407 Proxy Authentication Required`: the Session gave it no credentials, or it refused those of `proxy.username` and `proxy.password`. The details name the proxy and the username, never the password. Fix the credentials; retrying with the same ones fails the same way.
error_codes.name: proxy_auth_failed

error_codes.description: The Session's Proxy provider answered through its proxy with a failure of its own: its traffic quota or balance is spent (`quota_exhausted`), the Session's sticky exit is gone (`sticky_session_expired`), or a failure Goodfetch does not recognize (`unrecognized`, whose text is logged, never returned). The details name the provider, the proxy and the failure, never the credentials. A provider's refusal of the credentials is `proxy_auth_failed` instead. Retry later, or open a new Session for a new exit.
error_codes.name: proxy_provider_unavailable

error_codes.description: The engine could not open the loopback relay a Session's proxy goes through, such as when the machine has no free local port: the proxy itself was never tried. The details name the proxy, never its credentials, and the local error. Retry once the machine frees ports or file descriptors.
error_codes.name: proxy_relay_unavailable

error_codes.description: The Session's proxy could not be reached, its TLS failed, or it refused the tunnel or the request with an error of its own: the details name the proxy, never its credentials, and the browser's network error when it named one. It is the proxy's failure, never the site's and never `navigation_failed`: retry later, or through another proxy.
error_codes.name: proxy_unavailable

error_codes.description: The engine ran out of memory or storage for the Run: it checkpointed and stopped it, or refused to start it where its run file would go. The details name the `resource`. Resume it once memory or space frees up, on an engine with a larger allowance, or with lower ceilings.
error_codes.name: resources_exhausted

error_codes.description: A body or JSON the engine read from outside passed one of its limits, so the engine stopped reading it: more decoded bytes than `network.max_body_size`, more decoded bytes per received byte than `network.max_decompression_ratio` once past 1 MiB, or JSON nested deeper than `network.max_json_depth`. The details name the URL, the setting and its value; raise the setting for a site you trust.
error_codes.name: response_limit_exceeded

error_codes.description: The response's body is not JSON, or not the JSON the program reads it as: `json()` reads the body as UTF-8 whatever its charset, a leading BOM ignored. The SDK raises it itself, naming the response's URL; the body is the same on every read, so read it with `text()` or `body()` instead.
error_codes.name: response_not_json

error_codes.description: The response's body broke off before its end: shorter than its `Content-Length`, a chunked body without its last chunk, or a stream the server or the connection ended. A navigation waiting for `domcontentloaded` or `load` raises it for its main document; one that answered at `commit` leaves it to the body's read. The details name the URL and the bytes received and expected.
error_codes.name: response_truncated

error_codes.description: The route's request was answered already, by an earlier `continue`, `fulfill`, `abort` or `fallback`, or its handler ended: the first answer stands and this one changed nothing.
error_codes.name: route_already_handled

error_codes.description: Another engine holds the Run's writer lock, and the owner the Run index names did not say it took the action: it did not answer, and may still be taking it, or does not own the Run. The engine retried the lock 5 times over about a second; the writer may end, so try again later.
error_codes.name: run_busy

error_codes.description: The Run ID names a Run started with other inputs, or by another caller; the details list each difference. Start under another Run ID.
error_codes.name: run_conflict

error_codes.description: The Run ended `finished`, so it takes no new work, such as a page or a Session it would open: start a Run under a new Run ID. The details name the Run.
error_codes.name: run_ended

error_codes.description: The Run ID is not one the engine takes: lowercase letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, at most 128, starting and ending with a letter or a digit, never a name Windows reserves for a device.
error_codes.name: run_id_invalid

error_codes.description: Another engine holds the Run's writer lock, so this one cannot write the Run; the other may end.
error_codes.name: run_in_use

error_codes.description: The Run has no live writer and has not ended, as after a crash, so it has no report and none comes: a start with its Run ID resumes it. The details name the Run.
error_codes.name: run_interrupted

error_codes.description: A resumed Run's data key does not open under the key-encryption key `run_state.key_reference` names, such as a Checkpoint moved to a machine whose own key is another: the key that wrapped it never travels with the Checkpoint. The details name the Run, the setting, the reference resolved and the reference that wrapped the key, never a value. Name the key that wrapped it, in project configuration or configuration, and resume again.
error_codes.name: run_key_mismatch

error_codes.description: The engine still runs the Run, so it cannot be discarded: stop it first with `run.stop` or `run.abort`, or let it finish, then discard it. The details name the Run.
error_codes.name: run_live

error_codes.description: No Run has this Run ID: the Run index does not list it.
error_codes.name: run_not_found

error_codes.description: The action was forwarded to this engine as the Run's owner, and this engine does not own the Run: the Run index named an engine that has since ended or restarted. The engine that forwarded it retries the Run's writer lock.
error_codes.name: run_not_owned

error_codes.description: The Run's state is missing, damaged or cannot be written at its location; the details give the path. The engine never starts afresh under that Run ID.
error_codes.name: run_state_unavailable

error_codes.description: The sample operation refused the text.
error_codes.name: sample_refused

error_codes.description: A Secret placeholder's value would go to a domain outside its binding's `domains`: the field's frame or the request's URL. The details name the placeholder, the reference and the domain, never a value.
error_codes.name: secret_domain_not_allowed

error_codes.description: A Secret placeholder's value would be typed or sent where other code may read it, or to a host reached through an invalid-certificate exception, so it was not resolved. The details name the placeholder, the reference, the domain and the `reason`, never a value.
error_codes.name: secret_input_refused

error_codes.description: A Secret provider gave no value for a reference: a missing variable, a locked keychain, an unreachable vault, the caller's `resolveSecret` missing or throwing, no answer within `timeout.secret`. `failure` says which, and the details name the placeholder or setting, the reference and the provider, never a value.
error_codes.name: secret_unavailable

error_codes.description: No scope binds the Secret placeholder a call names. `bound` lists the placeholders bound, never a value.
error_codes.name: secret_unbound

error_codes.description: The Run is bound to the machine its Session source is on, and this is another machine: its login would reach sites from a new IP under the same cookies. Resume it on its own machine, or serve its Session source through a Browser host.
error_codes.name: session_bound_to_machine

error_codes.description: A value of the wrong type or out of the setting's own range, an empty or unparsable deployment variable, or a settings file that does not parse.
error_codes.name: setting_invalid

error_codes.description: A value a lower layer locked or capped, outside a Recipe's exposed bounds, or one only a lower layer may set or widen, such as `tls.trusted_cas` from a run. `limit` names the setting and the layer that holds it.
error_codes.name: setting_locked

error_codes.description: A setting given where it cannot take effect: in a layer that may not hold it, such as `browser_cache.max_unused_age` outside user configuration and an Operator policy, or on a Run it does not apply to, such as a crawl's setting on a Collie Run.
error_codes.name: setting_not_applicable

error_codes.description: A key no Product knows, or an unknown `GOODFETCH_` variable. The message names the closest valid one.
error_codes.name: setting_unknown

error_codes.description: The site's preferences refused the navigation or the request before it left, or refused the document once its response arrived, leaving the page on a blank document: its robots.txt disallows the URL (`robots_txt`), its `Crawl-delay` asks for more than the crawl allows (`crawl_delay`), or a use signal it sends refuses the crawl's Purpose (`use_signals`). Only a crawl handler's page asks a site's preferences; a page a program opens never raises it. The details name the URL and the reason.
error_codes.name: site_preferences_refused

error_codes.description: The locator still matched several elements when the action's timeout passed, so the action did nothing. The details list every match, each with a locator that reaches it alone, and `limit` names the timeout's setting; a longer timeout would not fix the locator.
error_codes.name: target_not_unique

error_codes.description: The Connection already has as many calls in flight as the engine serves on one, which `max` gives, so the engine refused this call at once and did nothing for it; the calls in flight go on, and the engine still reads their `$/cancel`, their `$/credit` and the replies to its own requests. Make the call again once an earlier call ended, cancel the calls no longer needed, or open another Connection.
error_codes.name: too_many_calls

error_codes.description: The navigation followed as many redirects as it may and was redirected again, as a redirect loop is: the browser's count is 20 requests in a navigation's chain, its first included, so Chromium follows 19 redirects. The details name the first URL, the hops followed and the count. A retry meets the same chain.
error_codes.name: too_many_redirects

error_codes.description: `upgrade-files` does not upgrade from this major: one this release's upgrade paths do not list, whose message names the release to upgrade through first, or a newer major than the executable's, whose message says to upgrade. No file is changed.
error_codes.name: upgrade_source_unsupported

error_codes.description: The Key-value store refused the key or its value: a key must be 1 to 512 Unicode scalar values with no control character, and a value any JSON but null, which `get` answers for an absent key; remove a key with `delete`. Bytes are read with `getBytes` and JSON with `get`, never the other way. The SDK refuses a value that is not JSON before sending it, and a value the call's Standard Schema rejects, sent or read; a JSON Schema written by hand types the value as JSON and checks nothing. The details name the key, say which was refused and, for a value's content, its path as a JSON Pointer.
error_codes.name: value_invalid

error_groups.description: The program is wrong: its call, its settings or its own handler code. Fix the program.
error_groups.name: program

error_groups.description: A policy, a Limit, a lock or a person refused. Change a setting, raise the Limit or ask the operator.
error_groups.name: refused

error_groups.description: The page or site never reached the state the call needed. Read the Run trace; change the step, the wait or the Access mode.
error_groups.name: page

error_groups.description: The Model provider's answer was unusable. Change the model or the strategy.
error_groups.name: model

error_groups.description: The deadline passed. Raise it, or wait for the right thing.
error_groups.name: deadline_exceeded

error_groups.description: Something Goodfetch depends on is unreachable or gone. Retry, or fix the setup.
error_groups.name: unavailable

error_groups.description: A bug in Goodfetch. Report it.
error_groups.name: internal

events.description: A Pinned artifact the call needs is downloading into the Browser cache: the bytes received so far, out of those announced.
events.name: browser_cache.download_progress

events.description: The engine's Resource governor sampled: its Memory allowance and what set it, the memory the engine and its children use, the host's pressure, CPU and Tokio saturation, its level and what holds it there, and each kind's concurrency. Telemetry: a newer sample replaces an unsent one.
events.name: engine.system_info

events.description: The engine no longer holds the position the subscription resumes after: the events since are gone, and this gives the current state, every live Run's axes and every item of "Needs you", from which the stream continues.
events.name: events.resync

events.description: An item of "Needs you" appeared, changed or left the list: resolved, by a person or by its Run, or dismissed. Lossless: a subscription that falls behind next takes `events.resync`, which holds every item.
events.name: needs_you.changed

events.description: The page closed: the engine closed it, or its window was closed in the browser outside every Client. Sent on each `page.on` call that listens to `close`, just before that call answers.
events.name: page.close

events.description: The page wrote a message to its console, `ConsoleMessage`: its type, text and location. Sent on each `page.on` call that listens to `console`, the only time the engine reads the page's console.
events.name: page.console

events.description: The page crashed: its renderer, or its browser's process, which exited abnormally. Its calls in flight raised `page_crashed`, and so does each later call. Sent on each `page.on` call that listens to `crash`.
events.name: page.crash

events.description: The document of the page's main frame fired `DOMContentLoaded`. Sent on each `page.on` call that listens to `dom_content_loaded`.
events.name: page.dom_content_loaded

events.description: A navigation of the page reached a file the browser downloads instead of showing, such as a PDF: the navigation answers no response and the page keeps its document. Names the page, the file's URL and the name the browser suggests.
events.name: page.download

events.description: The document of the page's main frame fired `load`. Sent on each `page.on` call that listens to `load`.
events.name: page.load

events.description: An exception the page did not catch, `WebError`: its name, message and stack. Sent on each `page.on` call that listens to `page_error`.
events.name: page.page_error

events.description: The page opened a popup, `window.open()` or a link opening another window: a page of the same Session, already under its routes and its interception, published before the popup's first request leaves. Published while `page.on` listens to `popup`.
events.name: page.popup

events.description: The page sent a request, `Request`, once per hop of a redirect chain: its URL, method, headers, body, resource type, navigation flag and the hops before it. Sent on each `page.on` call that listens to `request`; a service worker's own requests are never a page's.
events.name: page.request

events.description: A request of the page failed, `Request` with its `failure`, as Playwright reports one: the browser's network error, such as `net::ERR_FAILED` for one a route aborted or `net::ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED`, and the Error code when the engine blocked it, such as `egress_refused`, so a refusal is never a timeout. A response whose body broke off fails too. Sent on each `page.on` call that listens to `request_failed`; the Run trace records each request the engine refused that no call waited on.
events.name: page.request_failed

events.description: A request of the page got its whole response, its body included. Sent on each `page.on` call that listens to `request_finished`.
events.name: page.request_finished

events.description: A request of the page got its response's head: the request and its response, whose body `response.body` reads, and which says whether a site's service worker supplied it. Sent on each `page.on` call that listens to `response`.
events.name: page.response

events.description: The page opened a WebSocket, whose frames and close follow as `web_socket.frame_sent`, `web_socket.frame_received` and `web_socket.close`. Sent, with those, on each `page.on` call that listens to `web_socket`.
events.name: page.web_socket

events.description: A Run is being aborted: it stops at its next safe point. Lossless.
events.name: run.aborting

events.description: A Run's Lifecycle, Verdict or Completeness changed: it started running, or it ended. Lossless: while a subscriber's queue is full, the Run waits.
events.name: run.axes_changed

events.description: A Checkpoint of a Run is being written: on `run.checkpoint`, a pause, a migration, a clean stop or the periodic `checkpoint.interval`. Lossless.
events.name: run.checkpointing

events.description: A Run is being migrated to another machine: it checkpoints, then stops. Lossless.
events.name: run.migrating

events.description: A Run's progress changed, such as the program's own status line, a Human pause beginning or ending, or its end. Telemetry: a newer value of the same Run replaces an unsent one.
events.name: run.progress

events.description: A Run is stopping at its next safe point, with its cause: an abort, a pause or a migration. Lossless.
events.name: run.stopping

events.description: A text was repeated.
events.name: sample.echoed

events.description: A page opened in the Session: one `session.new_page` or `run.new_page` opened, or a popup one of its pages opened. Published while `session.on` listens to `page`.
events.name: session.page

events.description: A page's WebSocket closed.
events.name: web_socket.close

events.description: A page's WebSocket received a message frame: its text, or a binary frame's bytes in Base64.
events.name: web_socket.frame_received

events.description: A page's WebSocket sent a message frame: its text, or a binary frame's bytes in Base64.
events.name: web_socket.frame_sent

exit_codes.description: The command did what it was asked.
exit_codes.name: success

exit_codes.description: A bug in Goodfetch. Report it.
exit_codes.name: internal

exit_codes.description: The command line is wrong: an unknown command or flag, or a bad value. Nothing reached the engine.
exit_codes.name: usage
