exit_codes.description: The program is wrong: its call, its settings or its own handler code. Fix the program.
exit_codes.name: program

exit_codes.description: A policy, a Limit, a lock or a person refused. Change a setting, raise the Limit or ask the operator.
exit_codes.name: refused

exit_codes.description: The page or site never reached the state the call needed. Read the Run trace; change the step, the wait or the Access mode.
exit_codes.name: page

exit_codes.description: The Model provider's answer was unusable. Change the model or the strategy.
exit_codes.name: model

exit_codes.description: The deadline passed. Raise it, or wait for the right thing.
exit_codes.name: deadline_exceeded

exit_codes.description: Something Goodfetch depends on is unreachable or gone. Retry, or fix the setup.
exit_codes.name: unavailable

exit_codes.description: The running engine's Product does not carry what was asked: a Client that needs Foxhound reached a Collie engine, or a call, a setting or a value only Foxhound carries reached one. Run it with Foxhound, which contains everything Collie does, or connect to a Foxhound engine.
exit_codes.name: not_in_product

exit_codes.description: The Daemon refused the command's `hello`: by protocol version (`protocol_version_unsupported`), or, while it could not hand over, by Product (`not_in_product`, whose own row is for a call refused after `hello`). Run the `daemon restart` the refusal's `fix` names, or upgrade the Client.
exit_codes.name: protocol_version_unsupported

exit_codes.description: The Browser host the engine reached is of a version this engine cannot drive. Upgrade the Browser host, which either Product's executable runs as its `browser-host` command.
exit_codes.name: browser_host_outdated

exit_codes.description: The path the program chose cannot be written for a reason the path causes: permission denied, a read-only filesystem, a folder at the path, a file where a parent folder should be, a name the filesystem refuses, a file too large for that filesystem, or a path not found once its parents are made. No partial file is left. Change the path.
exit_codes.name: path_not_writable

exit_codes.description: The bytes of a file could not be written: no space or quota left, or an I/O error, or any failure where the engine keeps its files. No partial file is left. Free space where the files go, or ask the Daemon's operator, then make the same call again.
exit_codes.name: file_write_failed

exit_codes.description: The engine ran out of memory or storage for the Run: it checkpointed and stopped it, or refused to start it where its run file would go. The details name the `resource`. Resume it once memory or space frees up, on an engine with a larger allowance, or with lower ceilings.
exit_codes.name: resources_exhausted

exit_codes.description: A Limit that covers the run has nothing left in its period; the details name its scope, its Usage kind, its period and when it starts again. Wait for the next period, or ask a person to raise it.
exit_codes.name: limit_reached

exit_codes.description: The Run ended `stopped`: a Limit, an abort, its timeout, a pause or the loss of its engine stopped it. Resume it by its Run ID.
exit_codes.name: run_stopped

exit_codes.description: `--require-verified` was given and the Run, or the Agent's Success check, ended with a Verdict other than `verified`: `rejected` or `needs_review`.
exit_codes.name: verdict_not_verified

exit_codes.description: `audit verify` found an entry that does not verify: the Audit log, or the export it was given, was edited, deleted from, reordered or truncated at the sequence its output names.
exit_codes.name: audit_log_not_intact

exit_codes.description: The command was interrupted (`SIGINT`, or `CTRL_BREAK_EVENT` on Windows): its call was cancelled, and the Run it started checkpointed and stopped, resumable by its Run ID.
exit_codes.name: interrupted

exit_codes.description: The command was sent `SIGTERM`: its call was cancelled, and the Run it started checkpointed and stopped, resumable by its Run ID.
exit_codes.name: terminated

handler_requests.description: Asks a dialog handler to answer one dialog its page opened, named by its `dialog_id`, with `dialog.accept` or `dialog.dismiss`. The handler replies once it ends: a dialog it did not answer falls through to the handler before, and past the last one gets its default. A failure reply gives the dialog its default unless it was answered, removes the handler and raises `page_handler_failed`.
handler_requests.name: dialog.handle

handler_requests.description: Asks a route's handler to answer one request its URL pattern matched, named by its `route_id`, with `route.continue`, `route.fulfill`, `route.abort`, `route.fallback`, or `route.fetch` then `route.fulfill`. The handler replies once it ends: a request it did not answer falls back. A failure reply aborts the request unless it was answered, removes the route and raises `page_handler_failed`.
handler_requests.name: route.handle

hook_stages.description: Before the sample operation repeats a text.
hook_stages.name: sample_before_echo

metrics.description: The memory the browsers the Resource governor counts used at its last sample, each process with its descendants, PSS on Linux, summed over every browser; 0 with none (ADR 0040).
metrics.name: goodfetch.browser.memory

metrics.description: The browsers the Daemon's Runs' pools recycled, by why: `pages`, after `governor.browser.recycle_pages`; `memory`, past `governor.browser.memory_cap`; `idle`, past `governor.browser.recycle_idle` with no open page; `shed`, by the Resource governor at critical (ADR 0040).
metrics.name: goodfetch.browser.recycled

metrics.description: The browsers the Daemon's Runs launched that run now, by kind: the pinned Chrome for Testing, its headless shell under `browser.headless_shell`, or the distribution's Chromium where no build is made.
metrics.name: goodfetch.browser.running

metrics.description: The Clients connected to the Daemon, by the surface each named in its `hello`.
metrics.name: goodfetch.client.connected

metrics.description: The Counted work the Daemon, or an Attached engine serving `ops.attached_address`, did, by Shared path and kind of work: what `xtask counts` holds to the Quality register's limits, per unit, on its benchmarks.
metrics.name: goodfetch.counted_work

metrics.description: 1 while the Daemon drains, taking no Run (ADR 0049), else 0.
metrics.name: goodfetch.daemon.draining

metrics.description: The panics in the engine, each a bug in Goodfetch with a crash report on the machine, by what it ended: a call, an attempt, a Page, a Session, a browser, a Run, a Connection or the engine (ADR 0148).
metrics.name: goodfetch.engine.panics

metrics.description: 1 for the reading that holds the resource governor above normal, 0 for the others: all 0 at normal (ADR 0040).
metrics.name: goodfetch.governor.pressure_source

metrics.description: The share of the resource governor's concurrency target in use, from 0 to 1, the highest of its kinds', on which the Helm chart's autoscaler scales the Daemons (ADRs 0040 and 0055).
metrics.name: goodfetch.governor.saturation

metrics.description: How many of each kind of work the resource governor admits at once now, between its floor and its ceiling (ADR 0040).
metrics.name: goodfetch.governor.target

metrics.description: The Daemon's live Runs, whose Lifecycle is `running`, by kind.
metrics.name: goodfetch.run.active

metrics.description: The Runs that ended on the Daemon, by kind, Lifecycle, Verdict and Completeness (ADR 0029).
metrics.name: goodfetch.run.ended

metrics.description: The rows each Run-state batch of a run file wrote as its writer committed it, one a write, at a Durability level that batches attempts (`run_state.batch.per_attempt: false`, ADR 0142).
metrics.name: goodfetch.run_state.batch_rows

metrics.description: The checkpoints of a run file's write-ahead log that could not copy the whole log into the file, or start the log again, because a reader held an old snapshot of it (ADR 0138).
metrics.name: goodfetch.run_state.blocked_checkpoints

metrics.description: The bytes the Frontiers of the Daemon's open Runs hold in memory beside their run files, summed over them: each visit a batch not committed yet made, and those committed that memory keeps within `run_state.memory.budget`, at a Durability level that batches attempts (`run_state.batch.per_attempt: false`, ADR 0142).
metrics.name: goodfetch.run_state.memory

metrics.description: The visited-set lookups a Frontier's memory could not answer and that read the run file, because memory does not hold every visit the file holds: the file held more than `run_state.memory.budget` keeps as the Run opened, or a visit left memory past it since. While memory holds every visit, a lookup reads nothing (ADR 0142).
metrics.name: goodfetch.run_state.spilled_lookups

metrics.description: The bytes the write-ahead logs of the Daemon's open run files hold, summed over them, each as of its writer's last commit. A run file's log stays under twice its checkpoint threshold (32 MiB) unless a reader holds an old snapshot of it (ADR 0138).
metrics.name: goodfetch.run_state.wal.size

metrics.description: Texts the sample operation repeated.
metrics.name: goodfetch.sample.echoes

metrics.description: The space left to the engine's user, in bytes, on each filesystem the Resource governor samples, at its last sample, labelled by what the filesystem holds; a filesystem holding several of them gives each its series (ADR 0122).
metrics.name: goodfetch.storage.available

metrics.description: The inodes left to the engine's user on each filesystem the Resource governor samples that reports them, at its last sample, labelled by what the filesystem holds (ADR 0122).
metrics.name: goodfetch.storage.inodes.available

metrics.description: The storage level of each filesystem the Resource governor samples, at its last sample: 0 `normal`, 1 `low`, 2 `critical`, labelled by what the filesystem holds. `/readyz` fails while run state's is 2 (ADR 0122).
metrics.name: goodfetch.storage.level

operations.description: Exports the user's Audit log: every entry in sequence, each with the hash that chains it to the one before it, the anchor first when `audit.retention` pruned its beginning. The CLI's `audit export` writes them as JSONL, one entry per line, which `audit verify --file` verifies off the machine.
operations.name: audit.export

operations.description: Verifies the user's Audit log: every entry's hash chains it to the one before it, and the head file names the last one. Answers that it is intact, or the first sequence that does not verify, so an edited, deleted, reordered or truncated entry, a truncated tail included, shows.
operations.name: audit.verify

operations.description: Pins the changed key that stopped a host with `certificate_changed` in place of its pin, in the caller's partition, and records the accepted change in the Audit log; answers the new pin. Refused unless the key is the change the store holds for the host. A person's answer: offered only in the interactive CLI prompt.
operations.name: certs.accept

operations.description: Removes the caller's pin of a host, and any change waiting for it, so its next connection under trust on first use pins again; nothing else removes a pin. A person's answer: offered only in the interactive CLI prompt.
operations.name: certs.forget

operations.description: Lists the caller's pins in the known-certificates store: each host whose invalid certificate was accepted on first use, the SHA-256 of its public key, when and by which Run. Another person's pins on a shared Daemon are never listed. A row the engine cannot read is listed without its hash; it stops its host as a changed key.
operations.name: certs.list

operations.description: Shows each setting's effective value, the layer that set it and the layer that locked it, from the built-in defaults, the Operator policy, user configuration, the project configuration given and the run layer: the Connection's own settings with the run values given over them, or a live Run's as it opened when `run_id` names one; and lists the keys only the other Product honours as that Product's.
operations.name: config.explain

operations.description: Reads the Operator policy of this engine's major: every entry of its `settings`, `lock` and `cap` tables, and its digest, which `config.policy_write` takes back. A person's entry: no agent surface offers it.
operations.name: config.policy_read

operations.description: Writes changes to the Operator policy in one atomic write, only if its digest is still the one `config.policy_read` gave, every other byte of the file kept, and records the values before and after in the Audit log; a changed digest answers `policy_conflict` and writes nothing. Every change, a tightened cap included, applies to new Runs: a Run resolves its settings once, as it opens. A person's entry: no agent surface offers it.
operations.name: config.policy_write

operations.description: Writes user-level values to user configuration in one atomic write, every other byte of the file kept, once the resolver accepts them under the Operator policy, and records the values before and after in the Audit log; they apply to new Runs. A person's entry: no agent surface offers it.
operations.name: config.user_write

operations.description: Sets the level of the engine's log events this Connection receives as `$/log` notifications, from the next one on: `off`, `error`, `warn`, `info`, `debug` or `trace`, as `hello`'s `log_level` set it first. Each Connection has its own. Log events are telemetry: one the Connection is too slow to receive is dropped, and the next counts it in `dropped`.
operations.name: connection.set_log_level

operations.description: Says whether the Daemon is live and ready to take a new Run, and why not: what its ops listener's `/livez` and `/readyz` answer with a status alone.
operations.name: daemon.health

operations.description: Says what the Daemon runs as, where it listens, how many Clients and live Runs it has, when it stops idle, and its live heap.
operations.name: daemon.status

operations.description: Stops the Daemon once it answered: its live Runs stop, each resumable from its own state, and its runtime file and socket are removed.
operations.name: daemon.stop

operations.description: Answers a dialog by accepting it, a prompt with `prompt_text`, or else its default value; it answers once the page closed the dialog.
operations.name: dialog.accept

operations.description: Answers a dialog by dismissing it, as its Cancel button does; it answers once the page closed the dialog.
operations.name: dialog.dismiss

operations.description: Saves a Download's file, which the engine keeps with its Run, whole or not at all. An Attached engine given the program's path writes it through a hidden temporary file beside it, synced and renamed over it, creating missing folders and replacing a file there; any other engine writes nothing on its own machine and sends the file in `$/chunk` notifications of at most 64 KiB, one per credit granted with `$/credit`, for the SDK to write. Answers the file's size and SHA-256. A path that cannot be written raises `path_not_writable`, and full or failing storage `file_write_failed`, leaving the path as it was.
operations.name: download.save_as

operations.description: Records how an Effect's body ended (ADR 0106), judged by whether the engine sent anything for it: a body that returned a value the Effect journal keeps is `done` and never runs again; one that did not, with nothing sent or repeatable, is `dropped`, and runs at its next declaration; one that sent something and is not repeatable is `uncertain` until a person reconciles it. A returned value larger than `effect.output.max_size` with nothing sent raises `effect_output_invalid`. Called by the SDKs' `run.effect` only.
operations.name: effect.close

operations.description: Declares an Effect (ADR 0106): writes its entry in the Run's Effect journal before its body starts and answers `perform` with the entry and an `idempotency_key`, or the journal's answer, `journal` with the output an earlier attempt or start returned or `reconciled` after a person's "it happened", when the body must not run. An uncertain Effect raises `effect_uncertain`; a key declared again in one attempt while its body runs or after its answer raises `effect_key_reused`; across attempts of one namespace, the call waits until a body still running under its key is judged. Called by the SDKs' `run.effect` only.
operations.name: effect.open

operations.description: Says which Product the engine runs as, its Product version and major, and the protocol version it speaks.
operations.name: engine.info

operations.description: Subscribes to the engine's events. The call stays in flight, sending its events in `$/events` batches, never more than the credits granted with `$/credit`, until it is cancelled. No producer waits for a subscription: a lossless event is never dropped unseen, and a subscription whose queue is full falls behind, dropping its queued lossless events, and next sends `events.resync`, then the stream. A telemetry event is coalesced with the unsent one of the same kind and scope, and counts it as `dropped`. Given `after`, the last event read, it resumes after it, or starts with `events.resync` when the engine no longer holds it or another engine instance gave it, as after a Daemon restart. Given `system_info`, it also takes the Resource governor's periodic `engine.system_info`.
operations.name: events.subscribe

operations.description: Removes a key from a live Run's Key-value store and answers whether it existed. Through a crawl attempt (`attempt`), the removal is staged with the attempt, and whether the key existed counts what the attempt staged.
operations.name: key_value_store.delete

operations.description: Answers the JSON value a Run's Key-value store holds for a key, as committed, or null when the key is absent. A key holding bytes fails with `value_invalid`, naming `getBytes`. Takes no writer lock, so it reads a Run no program holds without resuming it. Through a crawl attempt (`attempt`), it reads what the attempt staged first.
operations.name: key_value_store.get

operations.description: Answers the bytes and content type a Run's Key-value store holds for a key, as committed, or null when the key is absent. A key holding JSON fails with `value_invalid`, naming `get`. Takes no writer lock. Through a crawl attempt (`attempt`), it reads what the attempt staged first.
operations.name: key_value_store.get_bytes

operations.description: Sends the committed keys of a Run's Key-value store that start with `prefix`, in the order of their Unicode scalar values, in `$/key` notifications, one per credit granted with `$/credit`, then answers how many it sent. Takes no writer lock.
operations.name: key_value_store.keys

operations.description: Commits a JSON value for a key in a live Run's Key-value store, replacing the one it held: the last commit wins. A null value fails with `value_invalid`; remove a key with `delete`. Through a crawl attempt (`attempt`), the write is staged with the attempt and commits or is discarded with it; once the attempt ended, it fails with `attempt_ended`.
operations.name: key_value_store.set

operations.description: Commits bytes with their content type for a key in a live Run's Key-value store, replacing what it held: the last commit wins. Bytes over 1 MiB are kept as a file in the Run's folder, which its Checkpoints carry.
operations.name: key_value_store.set_bytes

operations.description: Clicks the element the locator matches once it is unique, visible, enabled, stable and receiving the click (the guard, ADR 0019); a click that lands on another element is cancelled and sent again, until `timeout.action` passes. A click that starts a navigation of the page answers once that navigation's document committed or it ended without one, within `timeout.navigation` (ADR 0085).
operations.name: locator.click

operations.description: Runs a page function, as `page.evaluate` does, with the array of every element the locator matches first, none included, and its one JSON argument second, and answers its result, awaited, as JSON; the elements stay in the page, so a result holding one raises `page_value_invalid`. A selector the page does not parse raises `invalid_params`, and an exception thrown in the page `page_function_failed`. A main-world call is marked in the Session's Provenance.
operations.name: locator.evaluate_all

operations.description: Replaces the text of the field the locator matches, once it is unique, visible, enabled and editable, with text the page receives as typed input, until `timeout.action` passes. An input whose value a person picks rather than types (a date, a time, a month, a week, a local date and time, a colour or a range) has its value set, firing `input` and `change`, and a value it does not take fails with `invalid_params`.
operations.name: locator.fill

operations.description: Focuses the element the locator matches, once it is unique, visible and enabled, and presses a key or a combination on it as a keyboard does, until `timeout.action` passes. A press that starts a navigation of the page answers once that navigation's document committed or it ended without one, within `timeout.navigation` (ADR 0085).
operations.name: locator.press

operations.description: Waits until the element the locator matches is in the state: attached or visible, one element; detached, none; hidden, none or one not visible. The locator is resolved again at each check, so a re-render that replaces its element changes nothing. Past its `timeout`, `timeout.wait` when the call gives none, several matches raise `target_not_unique` listing them, and anything else `deadline_exceeded` naming the state.
operations.name: locator.wait_for

operations.description: Waits until the number of elements the locator matches is within the count, and answers it. Past its `timeout`, `timeout.wait` when the call gives none, it fails with `deadline_exceeded`.
operations.name: locator.wait_for_count

operations.description: Waits, checking from when the call arrives, until a page function called with the one element the locator matches first and its one JSON argument second answers a truthy result, and answers that result as JSON, as `page.wait_for_function` does. The locator is resolved again at each check, so a re-render that replaces its element changes nothing, and a check while none or several elements match counts as falsy. A value outside JSON raises `page_value_invalid`, an exception thrown in the page `page_function_failed`, and a selector the page does not parse `invalid_params`. A main-world call is marked in the Session's Provenance. Past its `timeout`, `timeout.wait` when the call gives none, it fails with `deadline_exceeded`.
operations.name: locator.wait_for_function

operations.description: Adds a domain whose consent wall a Run met, or `*` for every domain, to `consent.domains` in user configuration, so the next runs accept its consent walls instead of raising `blocked` with `consent_required`, and records the answer in the Audit log with the warning of what the person takes on; answers whether it added it. One call, no confirmation asked. A domain that file lists already adds nothing; an Operator policy that locks `consent.domains` refuses it with `setting_locked`. A person's answer: offered only in the Kennel and the interactive CLI prompt. The `consent_wall` items it covers leave the list with `needs_you.changed`.
operations.name: needs_you.allow_consent_domain

operations.description: Adds a registrable domain, with its required reason, to `wall.denied_domains` in the Operator policy, creating the file when there is none, so no run reads past its Walls or refetches its pages whatever another layer allows (ADR 0052), and records the denial and its reason in the Audit log; answers whether it added it. One call, no confirmation asked. A managed Operator policy refuses it with `setting_locked`. A person's answer: offered only in the Kennel and the interactive CLI prompt. The `wall_refetch_stopped` item of the domain leaves the list with `needs_you.changed`.
operations.name: needs_you.deny_wall_domain

operations.description: Hides an item of "Needs you" whose source lets a person dismiss it, for every Client, and answers whether it did; an item the list no longer holds, or one only resolving it removes, stays as it is. The item leaves the list with `needs_you.changed`.
operations.name: needs_you.dismiss

operations.description: Lists what waits for a person across every Run in the Run index and the stores beside it, the longest waiting first, a page at a time: `after` takes the `next` of the page before. `kinds` keeps the items of those kinds. Each change after the answer arrives as `needs_you.changed` on the event stream.
operations.name: needs_you.list

operations.description: Removes a domain on which a Run's refetch stopped from the layer of `wall.refetch_domains` that lists it, user configuration or else the Operator policy, every other entry and byte of the file kept, and records the answer in the Audit log; answers whether it removed it. When only `*` covers the domain there, `instead_of_star` gives the registrable domains that replace `*`, and without it the call is refused with `invalid_params`. A domain only project configuration lists is changed in that file, never here. A managed Operator policy, or one that locks the key against user configuration, refuses it with `setting_locked`. A person's answer: offered only in the Kennel and the interactive CLI prompt. The `wall_refetch_stopped` item leaves the list with `needs_you.changed`.
operations.name: needs_you.remove_refetch_domain

operations.description: Registers a script, registered when the call arrives, that runs in the main world of every document the page loads afterwards, its frames' included, before the document's own scripts: the call stays in flight, and a navigation sent after it waits until the script is registered. A function is called with its one JSON argument. The Session's Provenance marks the main-world injection. Cancelling the call, as closing its `Subscription` does, removes the script; it answers when the page closes.
operations.name: page.add_init_script

operations.description: Reads a page body by its handle, for a Client that cannot read the handle's file: sends the body in `$/chunk` notifications of at most 64 KiB, one per credit granted with `$/credit`, then answers its size.
operations.name: page.body

operations.description: Closes the page, a popup as any other: its calls in flight raise `call_cancelled` naming the program, it emits `close`, and a later call on it raises `closed`, while closing it again changes nothing. Its `beforeunload` handlers do not run unless `run_before_unload` is set: the page then closes once they let it, a dialog they raise going to its dialog handlers, and the call answers without waiting for that.
operations.name: page.close

operations.description: Runs a page function in the page's main frame with its one JSON argument, in the main world, where the page's globals are, or in an isolated world the page neither sees nor hooks, and answers its result, awaited, as JSON; a result of `undefined` answers no value. A value outside JSON in the result raises `page_value_invalid` naming its path and kind, and an exception thrown in the page `page_function_failed`. It is no gesture: it runs beside the page's actions. A main-world call is marked in the Session's Provenance.
operations.name: page.evaluate

operations.description: Reads the formats a request names from the page's current document, each read from one serialization of it, and answers only those, with the document's URL, its base URL and, when a format it names is read from the main content (`markdown` of the main content or fit, `html` of the main content, `text`), whether the document has main content. A document with no main content answers those formats empty and `main_content: "none"`, a value. It needs neither layout nor pixels, so every tier serves it.
operations.name: page.formats

operations.description: Goes back one entry in the page's history and waits for its `load` event, answering the document's response, or none when there is no entry to go back to. The back/forward cache is off, so the document always loads again (ADR 0121).
operations.name: page.go_back

operations.description: Goes forward one entry in the page's history and waits for its `load` event, answering the document's response, or none when there is no entry to go forward to. The back/forward cache is off, so the document always loads again (ADR 0121).
operations.name: page.go_forward

operations.description: Navigates the page to a URL and waits for its document's `load` event, or the state `wait_until` names, answering the document's response: a 404 or a 500 is a response, a value. A file the browser downloads, such as a PDF, answers no response and emits `page.download`. A navigation that reaches no document raises `navigation_failed`, one another navigation supersedes before it committed `navigation_interrupted`, a redirect loop `too_many_redirects`, a document whose body broke off `response_truncated`, unless the navigation answered at `commit`, and one past its `timeout`, or `timeout.navigation` without one, `deadline_exceeded`.
operations.name: page.goto

operations.description: Listens to one of the page's events, armed when the call arrives: the call stays in flight, and the engine sends that event of the page on the call itself, in `$/events` batches naming it, never more than the credits granted it with `$/credit`, its positions counting the call's own events from 1. Only the Connection that armed it gets them, never the engine's shared event stream. Lossless: past 1,024 events unsent, as when its Client grants too few credits, the call raises `page_events_lost` once it sent those. Cancelling the call, as closing its `Subscription` does, removes the listener; it answers when the page closes or its Run ends, once it sent the events it holds. The page's console and uncaught exceptions, its out-of-process frames' included, are read only while a call listens to `console` or `page_error`.
operations.name: page.on

operations.description: Hands the page's JavaScript dialogs to the program, armed when the call arrives: Playwright's `page.on('dialog')`. The call stays in flight, and for each dialog the engine sends `dialog.handle`, which the handler answers with `dialog.accept` or `dialog.dismiss`. Later handlers come first and the first answer wins; a handler that ends without one falls through, and past the last one, or with none, an `alert`, `confirm` or `prompt` is dismissed and a `beforeunload` dialog accepted, so a handler that answers nothing never stalls the page. Cancelling the call removes the handler; a handler that fails ends it with `page_handler_failed`, the dialog getting its default.
operations.name: page.on_dialog

operations.description: Reads the named fields from the page's current document in one call and answers each one's value: a value field's from the first element its CSS or XPath locator finds, its text or one attribute, optionally a `match` group, then its Value transform; a list's from every element its locator finds; rows' from each element a base locator finds, each row one object of its fields read under that element. A value the page does not give is null, and `unread` names it with why: a row lacking a field keeps its other fields. It never waits: an absent element is an answer. It needs neither layout nor pixels, so every tier serves it, and in the browser it is one read of the page whatever the number of fields.
operations.name: page.read

operations.description: Loads the page's document again and waits for its `load` event, answering the document's response: a 404 or a 500 is a response, a value. A navigation that reaches no document raises `navigation_failed`, and one another navigation supersedes before it committed `navigation_interrupted`.
operations.name: page.reload

operations.description: Sends a request from inside the page's Session's browser, with its cookies, through the browser-fetch tier and the page's interception (its domain policy, never its routes), from a context no service worker controls, and answers the response whatever its status, a 429 included; `response.body` reads its kept body, and raises `response_truncated` for one that broke off. A count of redirects above 19 is refused with `setting_invalid`, a chain past its count raises `too_many_redirects`, and a body whose content coding fails to decode `navigation_failed`.
operations.name: page.request

operations.description: Routes the page's requests whose URL matches to the program, armed when the call arrives: the call stays in flight, and for each such request the engine sends `route.handle`, which the handler answers with `route.continue`, `route.fulfill`, `route.abort`, `route.fallback`, or `route.fetch` then `route.fulfill`. Page routes come before Session routes, later routes first, and the first answer wins; a handler that ends without one falls back, and past the last route the request goes on to the network, so an unanswered route never stalls a request. What a route sends on still passes the domain policy. Cancelling the call removes the route; a handler that fails ends it with `page_handler_failed`.
operations.name: page.route

operations.description: Runs a page function in the page's main frame, as `page.evaluate` does, again at each polling interval and in each new document, until its result is truthy, and answers that result as JSON. A value outside JSON raises `page_value_invalid`, an exception thrown in the page `page_function_failed`. A main-world call is marked in the Session's Provenance. Past its `timeout`, `timeout.wait` when the call gives none, it fails with `deadline_exceeded`.
operations.name: page.wait_for_function

operations.description: Waits until the page's document reached the load state: at once when it already did. `networkidle` is reached once the document fired `load` and no request of the page was in flight for 500 ms since, WebSocket and server-sent-event connections and a service worker's own requests left out. Past its `timeout`, `timeout.wait` when the call gives none, it fails with `deadline_exceeded`.
operations.name: page.wait_for_load_state

operations.description: Waits, armed when the call arrives, until the page sends a request whose URL matches, and answers it, so a request an action triggers is caught by a waiter sent before the action. Past its `timeout`, `timeout.wait` when the call gives none, it fails with `deadline_exceeded`.
operations.name: page.wait_for_request

operations.description: Waits, armed when the call arrives, until a request of the page whose URL matches has finished, a hop that a redirect ended included, and answers it with its response, whose body the engine reads and keeps, so `response.body` never fails for it but for a redirect's, which has none. A request that fails is not waited for. Past its `timeout`, `timeout.wait` when the call gives none, it fails with `deadline_exceeded`.
operations.name: page.wait_for_request_finished

operations.description: Waits, armed when the call arrives, until a request of the page whose URL matches gets its response, a redirect's included, and answers both, so a response an action triggers is caught by a waiter sent before the action, even one that arrives before the program awaits it. Past its `timeout`, `timeout.wait` when the call gives none, it fails with `deadline_exceeded`.
operations.name: page.wait_for_response

operations.description: Waits, armed when the call arrives, until the page's URL matches: at once when it already does, else on a committed navigation, then until its document reaches `wait_until`, or on a change within the document, a `pushState`, a `replaceState` or a hash change. Past its `timeout`, `timeout.wait` when the call gives none, it fails with `deadline_exceeded`.
operations.name: page.wait_for_url

operations.description: Reads the body of the response a page's request got, once the request finished, as a page body's handle: kept already for a response `page.wait_for_request_finished` answered, and otherwise read from the browser, on the session of the frame that loaded it. A body the browser no longer holds, or a redirect's, which has none, raises `body_unavailable`, whose fix names `page.wait_for_request_finished`; one that broke off raises `response_truncated`, never returned as whole. Past its `timeout`, `timeout.wait` when the call gives none, a request that has not ended fails it with `deadline_exceeded`; a page that ends under it raises what ended it, as a call on the page does.
operations.name: response.body

operations.description: Answers a route's request by failing it with a network error its page sees, `failed` unless named; nothing reaches the network.
operations.name: route.abort

operations.description: Answers a route's request by sending it on, with any overrides, past every other route: the domain policy judges what it sends.
operations.name: route.continue

operations.description: Answers a route's request by passing it, with any overrides, to the route registered before, from the page's first route to the Session's last; past the last route it goes on to the network.
operations.name: route.fallback

operations.description: Sends a route's request on, with any overrides, past every other route, as `route.continue` does, and answers the response it got, its body kept; the handler then answers the request with `route.fulfill`, or, ending without one, the page gets that response.
operations.name: route.fetch

operations.description: Answers a route's request with a response of the program's own, or the one `route.fetch` returned with its changes; nothing reaches the network.
operations.name: route.fulfill

operations.description: Stops a Run at its next safe point, `stopped` and `incomplete`: no attempt in flight commits, and its work items return to pending. Answers its Run report; an ended Run's report is answered as it is. A Run whose engine died is stopped by this engine, which takes its writer role at the next run epoch; a Run another engine writes is stopped by that engine, the owner the Run index names.
operations.name: run.abort

operations.description: Writes a Checkpoint of a live Run now, through SQLite's online backup, where `location` says or where the engine keeps the Run's Checkpoints, and answers it once its file is complete, with its size, digest, run epoch and journal position. A Checkpoint the engine cannot write fails with `file_write_failed` and leaves no file.
operations.name: run.checkpoint

operations.description: Discards a Run that ended or was interrupted, for good, so that nothing of it is left behind (ADRs 0001, 0002, 0015 and 0036): its wrapped data key is overwritten and its run folder removed, with its run file, page bodies, browser profiles and the Checkpoints written there; in the per-install layout its rows are deleted from the install database with `secure_delete` on, then `wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)`, so neither the database nor its `-wal` and `-shm` files hold its bytes. Its Run index row stays, marked `erased`, without its tags or status line. A Profile directory it used in place and a Borrowed browser are the person's own and are never touched (ADR 0056), nor are Checkpoints written elsewhere. A later `run.start` under its Run ID starts a new Run; discarding a Run already discarded changes nothing. A Run this engine runs fails with `run_live`, one whose writer lock another engine holds with `run_in_use`, and a Run ID no Run has with `run_not_found`.
operations.name: run.discard

operations.description: Lets a Run finish and answers its Run report: a Run its program drives ends at once, `finished` and `complete`; a crawl ends once its work items are done, and a keep-alive crawl (`crawl.keep_alive`), which waits for new work while nothing is left, ends once this call lets it and its work items are done. A Run something stopped first answers its report saying `stopped`. A Run that ended `failed` fails the call with the error that failed it, and a write at its end that failed, such as its Plan file's, with that write's error. Cancelling the call, or its `timeout` passing, which fails it with `deadline_exceeded`, ends only the wait.
operations.name: run.finish

operations.description: Lists the Runs of the Run index of the user and major, of either Product (ADRs 0031 and 0098): each row with its tags, Lifecycle, Verdict, Completeness, start and end, the engine that owns it while it is live, and its presence, a Run whose state is gone `missing` and one discarded on purpose `erased`, never left out. The engine filters by tags, the Recipe, Schedule, occurrence and trigger its reserved `goodfetch.` tags name, Product, each axis, start and end time, and a text found in its Run ID or tags, and sorts by the key given; Watch runs are left out unless `watch_runs` asks for them (ADR 0036).
operations.name: run.list

operations.description: Migrates a live Run: checkpoints it where `location` says or where the engine keeps its Checkpoints, then stops it at its next safe point, `stopped` with the stop reason `migrate`, to be resumed from that Checkpoint on another machine. Answers its Run report, which names the Checkpoint.
operations.name: run.migrate

operations.description: Opens a page in the Run's default Session, which the first call opens with the Run's settings and every later call shares; `page.session()` reaches it. The first page launches the Run's browser, so a missing browser build raises its code from this call.
operations.name: run.new_page

operations.description: Opens a Session of the Run's own: its own browser context, with its own cookies, storage, identity and proxy, sharing the Run's browser process, so two Sessions of a Run never share a login. It opens from `source`, or else from the Run's `session.source`, or fresh; `session.source` in its own `settings` is refused with `setting_not_applicable`. The Run's first Session launches its browser, so a missing browser build raises its code from this call.
operations.name: run.new_session

operations.description: Pauses a live Run: checkpoints it, then stops it at its next safe point, `stopped` with the stop reason `pause` and resumable by its Run ID with `run.resume`, after a restart too. Answers its Run report, which names the Checkpoint.
operations.name: run.pause

operations.description: Reads a Run's progress: what it does and why it waits. Without `after`, it answers at once; given `after`, the position of the value the reader last read, it waits for a change and answers the latest value, so values in between are coalesced. The value whose `last` is true ends the sequence: the Run ended, and its `lifecycle` and `stop_reason` say how, or no engine works it (`writer: none`) until a start with its Run ID resumes it. A Run another engine works is read through that engine, the owner the Run index names, and one no engine works from its committed state; a read never takes the Run's writer lock. A Run ID the Run index does not list fails with `run_not_found`.
operations.name: run.progress

operations.description: Reads a Run's report: at once for a Run that ended, and at its end for a live one, which the read never ends. A Run another engine works is read through that engine, and one no engine works from its committed state, never taking its writer lock. A Run that has no live writer and has not ended fails with `run_interrupted`, whose `fix` names a start with its Run ID, and a Run ID the Run index does not list with `run_not_found`.
operations.name: run.report

operations.description: Resumes an interrupted Run from its committed state, its run file on this machine or the Checkpoint `checkpoint` names: it takes the Run's writer lock and the next run epoch, so every write of an earlier writer is refused, and redoes the work since that state; its recorded Clean-up rules digest is kept. A Run this engine runs already fails with `run_in_use`, as one another engine writes does; a finished one is answered as it ended, `ended`. A Run bound to another machine fails with `session_bound_to_machine`, and a Checkpoint of a format version this engine cannot read with `format_version_unsupported`.
operations.name: run.resume

operations.description: Sets the program's own status line about a live Run, at most 512 characters, which replaces the one before: kept in the Run's state, so a resume keeps it, shown in its Run index row and carried on its progress, `run.progress`. Answers the Run's progress. A Run this engine does not run fails with `run_not_found`.
operations.name: run.set_progress_message

operations.description: Starts a Run its program drives, and answers once it is started. A Run ID names the Run for good, and a start under one acts on what the Run index holds (ADR 0102): no such Run begins it, `new`; an interrupted Run, stopped, failed, or running with no live writer, resumes from its committed state at the next run epoch, `resumed`, as `run.resume` does; a finished Run is answered as it ended with no handler called, `ended`. A Run live with a writer, in this engine or another, fails with `run_in_use`; a Run started with other inputs or by another caller with `run_conflict` listing each difference; a Run the Run index lists whose state is missing or unreadable with `run_state_unavailable`, never starting afresh.
operations.name: run.start

operations.description: Answers whether the start that opened the Run's handle began the Run, `new`, resumed it, `resumed`, or found it ended, `ended` (ADR 0102). The handle answers it from that start's answer, without a message to the engine.
operations.name: run.started_as

operations.description: Stops a Run at its next safe point with a Checkpoint, `stopped` and `incomplete` as an abort by its program, resumable by its Run ID, and answers its Run report; an ended Run's report is answered as it is. The wait is bounded by `timeout.close`, or the call's `timeout`: past it, the call fails with `deadline_exceeded` and the Run still stops at its next safe point. A Run that ended `failed` fails the call as `run.finish` does.
operations.name: run.stop

operations.description: Answers what a Run used, as the Usage ledger charged it: its model calls and tokens, browser time, proxy bytes, requests, paid solves and Paid fetches, each Limit that applies to it with what is left of it, and whether it is uncapped. An ended Run answers its report's Usage.
operations.name: run.usage

deprecated.note: A sample entry, which the real catalog replaces.

operations.description: Repeats a text back to the caller.
operations.name: sample.echo

operations.description: Closes the Session: its pages and its browser context close, and its pages' admissions go back to the Resource governor; a Borrowed browser is never closed. A later call on the Session or one of its pages raises `closed`, and closing it again changes nothing.
operations.name: session.close

operations.description: Opens a page in the Session, with its cookies and storage, and its own settings. Once the Session is closed, it raises `closed`.
operations.name: session.new_page

operations.description: Listens to one of the Session's events, armed when the call arrives: the call stays in flight, and the engine publishes that event of the Session on its event stream, lossless, which `events.subscribe` reads under its credits. Cancelling the call removes the listener; it answers when the Session closes or its Run ends.
operations.name: session.on

operations.description: Lists the Session's open pages, in the order they opened: those the program opened and the popups its pages opened. Once the Session is closed, it raises `closed`.
operations.name: session.pages

operations.description: Routes the requests of every page of the Session whose URL matches to the program, as `page.route` does, after the page's own routes.
operations.name: session.route

operations.description: Makes a new Ed25519 key for an `identified` Session's Web Bot Auth signatures, from the OS generator, and keeps it as a private JSON Web Key in the item a `keychain:` or `secretfile:` Secret reference names; answers the reference, the key's ID and its public key, never the private key. An item that holds an Ed25519 key already keeps it and answers it with `created` false; one that holds anything else is refused. Set `identified.signing_key` to the reference, then export the key directory with `signing_key.directory`.
operations.name: signing_key.create

operations.description: Exports the Web Bot Auth key directory of the keys the Secret references name, for the user to serve at `/.well-known/http-message-signatures-directory` of the origin `identified.signature_agent` names: the body, a JSON key set of each key's public JSON Web Key named by its RFC 7638 thumbprint, and the `Content-Type`, `Signature-Input` and `Signature` fields its response carries, where each key signs the origin's authority with the tag `http-message-signatures-directory` to prove it holds the key. Valid for `valid_for` milliseconds, seven days by default; export it again before `expires`. A reference that gives no Ed25519 private JSON Web Key is refused.
operations.name: signing_key.directory

operations.description: Lists every Limit of the Usage ledger, by scope, with the Usage charged and held against it in its current period and what is left.
operations.name: usage.list

operations.description: Sets a Limit to a person's amount, in place of every Limit of its scope, Usage kind, currency and period but a managed Operator policy's, keeping the Usage counted. A person's answer: offered only in the Kennel and the interactive CLI prompt.
operations.name: usage.raise

operations.description: Adds a Limit of the caller's own to the Usage ledger, which holds beside the others: the tightest one holds, so it can only lower what applies. Answers it with its Usage.
operations.name: usage.set

plugin_kinds.description: Keeps values by key for the sample operations.

methods.description: Keeps a value under a key.
methods.name: put

plugin_kinds.name: sample_store

settings.description: How many requests a Run admits in a minute at most, spaced evenly (GCRA), whatever its concurrency; none by default. An Operator policy cap bounds it even when unset.
settings.name: admission.max_requests_per_minute

settings.description: Whether an engine process also sends each new Audit log entry, the hash with it, as an OpenTelemetry event to the OTLP/HTTP collector `otlp.logs_endpoint` names: off by default, and nothing is sent while `otlp.logs_endpoint` is unset. Read when the process starts; set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.
settings.name: audit.otlp

settings.description: How many of one listener's refusals the Audit log records in a minute, from its first: 10. Each refusal past them is still logged, and once the minute ends one `endpoint_refusals_folded` entry counts them, so a peer that retries a wrong token cannot make the engine write an entry per attempt. 0 records none but the counts. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.
settings.name: audit.refusals_per_minute

settings.description: How long the user's Audit log keeps an entry, in milliseconds, such as 15552000000 for the six months the EU AI Act asks of high-risk deployers. Unset, the default, nothing is ever pruned. Set, the engine prunes the entries older than it as it starts and then once a day, so an entry may stay up to a day longer, from the log's beginning only, leaving an anchor entry that carries the last pruned hash, from which `audit verify` checks the rest, and a pruning record at the tail. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.
settings.name: audit.retention

settings.description: The Access mode a Session opens in and keeps for its life: `standard` (the default), the browser's own identity; `identified`, which declares who the program is, signing each request it sends with `identified.signing_key` (Web Bot Auth), and masks nothing; or `stealth`, which turns on the whole stealth catalog, each `stealth.*` item of which can be switched off. A non-`none` `stealth.fingerprint_method` makes the Session `stealth`; an explicit `standard` or `identified` beside one at the same scope is `setting_invalid` naming both keys. A stealth item set explicitly where a `standard` Session opens is `setting_not_applicable`, and one set explicitly on an `identified` Session is `setting_invalid` naming both keys; an inherited one yields, which `config explain` names in the item's `yields_to`. `stealth` on WebKit is `capability_unavailable`; a Borrowed browser stays `standard` with its own identity, and `stealth` set where one opens is `setting_not_applicable`, as is `identified` at an import or on a Profile directory used in place. Changing the mode, the Identity profile or the proxy means opening a new Session. A Label refuses it with `setting_not_applicable`.
settings.name: browser.access_mode

settings.description: The resource kinds the Session's pages never load, failed as `BlockedByClient` by its interception before every navigation: any of `image`, `media`, `font` and `stylesheet`; none by default. The never-block list still loads a challenge's own. In `standard` and `stealth` the Run warns once per Session that the site can see the missing loads.
settings.name: browser.block_resources

settings.description: Whether the Run trace keeps its CDP command log, `trace/cdp-commands.jsonl`: one line for each command the engine sends a Session's browser, its method only, never its params, up to the launch's last `Browser.close`. Off by default: no command's method goes to the Run trace's writer and the file is never written. Turn it on to see every command the engine sent, such as to debug a Run. No result, Record or Provenance entry reads the log, so off weakens no guarantee.
settings.name: browser.cdp_command_log

settings.description: Whether the Session's Chromium runs with no window: `true` by default. Headless or not, the site sees one browser's identity, with no `HeadlessChrome` token in its user agent, except under `browser.headless_shell`.
settings.name: browser.headless

settings.description: Whether the Session's Chromium is Chrome for Testing's `chrome-headless-shell` build, of the same pinned release, in place of the full browser: `false` by default. The shell runs only headless and differs from the full browser in fingerprint and features: a site sees its own identity, `HeadlessChrome` in its user agent and client hints, where the full build shows its window's. It starts where the full browser's headless mode cannot, such as on macOS with no GUI session (`browser_needs_gui_session`). It is downloaded on first use, as the full build is. Refused with `setting_not_applicable` beside `browser.headless: false`, and under the `stealth` Access mode, which launches its own build; a Borrowed browser launches nothing, so it takes no effect there.
settings.name: browser.headless_shell

settings.description: Whether a site's service workers run in the Session's pages: `allow` (the default on Chromium) runs them under the Session's interception, each worker's own requests passing the domain policy, the Filter lists and the Session's routes, never a page's routes; `block` makes `navigator.serviceWorker.register()` reject as on a failed fetch of the worker's script, `register` staying the browser's own function, so that every request of a page reaches its routes.
settings.name: browser.service_workers

settings.description: How long a Pinned artifact no installed executable pins stays in the Browser cache unused before the clean-up deletes it, and how long an executable's entry counts as installed after it was last seen: 30 days. `null` turns the automatic clean-up off. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.
settings.name: browser_cache.max_unused_age

settings.description: How often a live Run writes a Checkpoint where the engine keeps its Checkpoints, on the engine's clock; none by default locally.
settings.name: checkpoint.interval

settings.description: The OCI repository the daily channel is pulled from, `host[:port]/path`: Goodfetch's own on ghcr.io by default, or a mirror of it, which `clean_up.update = daily` makes the configured destination. Only Operator policy and user and project configuration set it: a Recipe's or a run's value is `setting_locked`.
settings.name: clean_up.channel

settings.description: How long fetching a version of the Clean-up rules from its sources may take at a Run's start or resume: past it, a Run holds to the newest version this machine has, and a `clean_up.version` it cannot fetch refuses the start. 30 s.
settings.name: clean_up.fetch_timeout

settings.description: The URL `clean_up.update = upstream` fetches each Filter list from, by list: `ads` (EasyList), `trackers` (EasyPrivacy), `annoyances` (Fanboy Annoyance) and `unbreak` (Brave's unbreak list); their authors' own URLs by default, or a mirror's. Each must be `https`. Only Operator policy and user and project configuration set it: a Recipe's or a run's value is `setting_locked`.
settings.name: clean_up.lists

settings.description: Where a new Run's Clean-up rules come from: `release` (the default), the set this release pins, with the embedded part as fallback; `daily`, the opt-in daily channel, whose registry it makes a configured destination, refused with `capability_unavailable` until the engine checks the channel's signature; `upstream`, the Filter lists from their authors' URLs, which it makes configured destinations. A Run holds to the version it starts with for its whole life, a resume included; `egress.offline` turns the fetching off. Operator policy can lock it.
settings.name: clean_up.update

settings.description: The exact version of the Clean-up rules a new Run holds to, by its digest `sha256:<hex>` as Provenance names it, instead of the newest one `clean_up.update` gives: a daily version it names is fetched from the daily channel, and it is exempt from the channel's expiry and its refusal of older versions. None by default.
settings.name: clean_up.version

settings.description: The most events the Client holds for one listener that has not taken them yet, a whole number from 1: 1024 by default. Past it the listener loses the events that follow; once it has taken those it held, it is removed and ends with `listener_events_lost` naming how many it lost, and the other listeners go on. The TypeScript Client applies it to its own transport. Set in `connect()`'s own `settings` only.
settings.name: connection.max_listener_queue

settings.description: The most calls the Client holds waiting for their answer, a whole number from 1: 10000 by default. A call past it is refused at once, unsent, with `connection_overloaded` and the bound `pending_calls`; the calls made before it go on. The TypeScript, Python and Rust Clients apply it to their own transport from their first call, `hello` included. Set in `connect()`'s own `settings` only.
settings.name: connection.max_pending_calls

settings.description: The most bytes the Client holds waiting to be written to the engine, a whole number from 1: 64 MiB (67108864) by default. While bytes wait, a call whose message would pass it is refused at once, unsent, with `connection_overloaded` and the bound `queued_write_bytes`; the calls made before it go on, and one message larger than the bound is still taken while nothing waits. The TypeScript, Python and Rust Clients apply it to their own transport from their first call, `hello` included. Set in `connect()`'s own `settings` only.
settings.name: connection.max_queued_write_bytes

settings.description: The registrable domains on which a run accepts a consent wall, a Consent prompt with no refusal that covers the content or offers payment instead, rather than raising `blocked` with `consent_required`; `*` only when written. A prompt that offers a refusal is still refused there. A Recipe or a run only narrows it; it is widened only in an Operator policy, user or project configuration, or by a person's answer.
settings.name: consent.domains

settings.description: What a browser Session does with Consent prompts: `answer` (the default, in every Access mode) refuses each prompt in every frame and hides one with no refusal that leaves the content readable; `detect` only looks: nothing is clicked or hidden, the wall test still runs, and a consent wall is still `consent_required`; `off` registers and starts no Consent prompt runner and lets no cosmetic rule act on the live page or in extracted content, so no consent wall is reported and the page's text is returned as served, while the Filter lists still block requests; the Run report lists `off` in `weakened`. A Recipe, and a Client acting for a model, never set `off` unless the layers below already give it: `setting_locked`; set it in the program's own code, in configuration or in an Operator policy.
settings.name: consent.handling

settings.description: What a consent wall on a domain outside `consent.domains` does: `report` (the default) leaves the page at `consent_required`, raised as `blocked`; `ask` raises a Human pause for a person's answer, for this run or always for the domain. Until the Human pause takes a person's answer, `ask` opens no page: `capability_unavailable`.
settings.name: consent.on_wall

settings.description: The main-content step `page.formats` reads a page's main content with, before its Markdown, its main HTML and its text: `dom_smoothie` (the default), Readability's algorithm, or `trafilatura`, the rs-trafilatura port. A step that finds no text in a document holding text outside its navigation landmarks answers that text. Set at any scope down to a page: a Run, a Session's or a page's own `settings`.
settings.name: content.extractor

settings.description: Where `daemon run`, the foreground Daemon, listens, as `host:port`: `127.0.0.1` on port 7900 plus the major (7600 plus the minor during `0.y` previews). Port 0 takes a free port, which its log names. Only a loopback address, until the Daemon terminates TLS. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy, or for `daemon run` through `GOODFETCH_DAEMON_ADDRESS`.
settings.name: daemon.address

settings.description: How long `daemon run`, the foreground Daemon, drains on `SIGTERM` before it exits: 110 seconds, below the 120-second `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` of the Helm chart, which must exceed it. Each run that reaches its next safe point in that time stops with a Checkpoint, resumable by its Run ID; one that does not stays resumable from its run file. Any Daemon whose listener is closed for good drains the same way within it, then exits 1. An Attached engine that stops on a panic in a part every run shares waits as long for its runs to stop, leaving each one not stopped resumable from its run file, then exits 1. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy, or for `daemon run` through `GOODFETCH_DAEMON_DRAIN_GRACE` in milliseconds.
settings.name: daemon.drain_grace

settings.description: How long a Daemon with no connected Client waits before it stops: 10 minutes. `daemon start --keep-alive`, a held Schedule and an installed service keep it running. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.
settings.name: daemon.idle_timeout

settings.description: The most bytes of JSON an Effect's body may return for the Effect journal to keep (ADR 0106), 64 KiB by default as `crawl.payload.max_size`. A larger value is `effect_output_invalid` when nothing was sent, and leaves the Effect uncertain after a send.
settings.name: effect.output.max_size

settings.description: The hosts a run's requests may reach: each entry its host and their subdomains, matched on the host as a browser's URL parser leaves it (punycode, dotted-decimal IPv4), and `*` every host, only when written. `["*"]` by default; set for a connection or a Run, and only narrowed by a Recipe or a Client acting for a model, whose value listing a host the value below does not cover is `setting_locked`. A request to a host it does not list fails with `egress_refused`.
settings.name: egress.allowed_domains

settings.description: The hosts no request of a run may reach, whatever `egress.allowed_domains` allows: each entry its host and their subdomains, matched as `egress.allowed_domains` matches, and `*` every host. Empty by default; set for a connection or a Run, and only added to by a Recipe or a Client acting for a model, whose value that leaves a host the value below lists uncovered is `setting_locked`. A request to a host it lists fails with `egress_refused`.
settings.name: egress.blocked_domains

settings.description: The addresses a Session's connections and DNS queries leave from (ADR 0044): a list of the host's IP addresses, such as `["192.0.2.10", "2001:db8::10"]`, a network interface's name, such as `eth0`, whose addresses are read when each Session starts, or an IPv6 prefix, such as `2001:db8:1::/48`. Each Session binds one address of each IP family for its life, new Sessions spread round-robin across the blocks `egress.rotation_block.ipv4` and `.ipv6` size. A prefix covers the host's addresses inside it, and on Linux any address of it once `net.ipv6.ip_nonlocal_bind` is 1 and the prefix is routed locally. A value that yields no address the host can use refuses the run with `local_address_unavailable`, and a site with no address in a family the Session holds fails with `address_family_unavailable`. None by default: the address the OS chooses. A Recipe may expose it but never sets it, since its addresses are the machine's own.
settings.name: egress.local_addresses

oneOf.description: IP addresses of the host.
An interface's name, such as `eth0`, or an IPv6 prefix, such as `2001:db8:1::/48`.

settings.description: Whether Operator-configured endpoints (Model providers, Secret providers, proxies, Notification webhooks, OTLP collectors, the Plugin index, a configured `cdp_url`) are refused every address that is not globally reachable, as the addresses a page can reach are, so a tenant's endpoint never reaches the network the engine runs in. `false` by default, so an endpoint on localhost or a private network works; set only in an Operator policy, as Goodfetch Cloud sets it. A refused endpoint fails with `egress_refused` before it connects.
settings.name: egress.no_private_endpoints

settings.description: Whether the engine opens no connection nobody configured: every pinned download, such as a Pinned artifact missing from the Browser cache, fails with `artifact_unavailable_offline` before it connects, naming the command that supplies it beforehand. `false` by default; set at every layer, and an Operator policy can lock it.
settings.name: egress.offline

settings.description: The ranges and hosts that addresses a page can reach may use although they are not globally reachable, for tests against a local site or an intranet: CIDR ranges such as `127.0.0.0/8`, IP addresses, and host names, each name's connections allowed any address that is not globally reachable. A cloud-metadata address (`169.254.169.254`, `fd00:ec2::254`, `100.100.100.200`) is reached only when listed by its exact address, never through a range or a host name that covers it. Empty by default; set by the program's own code, configuration or an Operator policy, by a Recipe only where the Operator policy's `egress.recipe_private_ranges` allows it, and never by a Client acting for a model, whose value is `setting_locked`. A run that lists any records it once in the Audit log as `private_addresses_allowed` and in its Run report's `weakened`.
settings.name: egress.private_ranges

items.description: A CIDR range such as `127.0.0.0/8`, an IP address such as `169.254.169.254`, or a host name such as `intranet.example`.

settings.description: Whether a Recipe may set `egress.private_ranges`. `false` by default, so a Recipe's value is `setting_locked`; set only in an Operator policy.
settings.name: egress.recipe_private_ranges

settings.description: The prefix length of the IPv4 blocks new Sessions are spread across, round-robin, when `egress.local_addresses` gives several: 24 by default, so consecutive Sessions leave from different /24 networks while the addresses allow it. Set for a connection or a Run.
settings.name: egress.rotation_block.ipv4

settings.description: The prefix length of the IPv6 blocks new Sessions are spread across, round-robin, when `egress.local_addresses` gives several: 64 by default, the block a rate limiter such as Cloudflare's counts as one client. Set for a connection or a Run.
settings.name: egress.rotation_block.ipv6

settings.description: How many times the main-content step may try a page. `retry` (the default) tries up to four times while it finds under 500 characters, keeping the best. `single_attempt` tries once, which is faster and may keep less text on short pages. The trafilatura Extractor always tries once.
settings.name: extraction.readability

settings.description: How a `page.formats` call that read its main content measures the share of that text the Clean-up rules removed, which its Provenance entry records, flagged above a fifth: `estimate` (the default), the text removed over that text plus the main content's text left, an upper bound of the exact share that runs no second main-content step; or `exact`, the main content's text of the page as served against the cleaned page's, at the cost of one more main-content step. The entry names the measure it holds.
settings.name: extraction.removal_share

settings.description: Whether a browser Session blocks ads by EasyList, as a blocker does: on by default in every Access mode. A blocked request fails as `BlockedByClient`; the never-block list keeps challenge, anti-bot, anti-fraud and payment scripts loading.
settings.name: filter_lists.ads

settings.description: Whether a browser Session blocks page annoyances (social widgets, newsletter and notification prompts) by Fanboy Annoyance, its cookie sections left to the Consent prompt runner: on by default in every Access mode.
settings.name: filter_lists.annoyances

settings.description: Extra Filter lists, by URL or path. Their scriptlets run only when the value comes from an Operator policy or user or project configuration; from a Recipe or a run, only their blocking rules apply.
settings.name: filter_lists.extra

settings.description: Whether a site's own scripts load whatever the Filter lists say: off by default.
settings.name: filter_lists.first_party_scripts

settings.description: How many hosts' Clean-up rules this Run keeps built: 1,024, the least used dropped first, and none once the Resource governor finds memory critical. A page on a host it keeps builds no rule list. 0 builds each page's rule list, as before.
settings.name: filter_lists.host_cache

settings.description: Whether the Filter lists' scriptlets that patch a page's JavaScript run, from uBlock Origin's resources downloaded with the lists that name them: off by default, since a site can see them.
settings.name: filter_lists.page_scriptlets

settings.description: Whether a browser Session blocks trackers by EasyPrivacy: on by default in every Access mode. A blocked request fails as `BlockedByClient`; the never-block list keeps challenge, anti-bot, anti-fraud and payment scripts loading.
settings.name: filter_lists.trackers

settings.description: The most threads the engine starts for work that waits on the operating system, such as reading files: `per_core` for one a core, or a whole number of at least 1. Each such thread holds its own stack; a Page analysis never runs on one. Read once, when the engine starts.
settings.name: governor.blocking_threads

oneOf.description: This many threads.
One thread a core.

settings.description: How many of a Run's Sessions share one browser process, each in a browser context of its own: 8. The Run's next Session past it gets a process of its own; Sessions of different Runs never share one.
settings.name: governor.browser.contexts_per_process

settings.description: The memory, in bytes, of a browser and its processes past which it is recycled; unset by default, when the cap is twice what the browser used once it had opened its first page.
settings.name: governor.browser.memory_cap

settings.description: The memory, in bytes, of one page's JavaScript heap and the buffers it holds, past which the Resource governor ends the page while memory is critical: 1 GiB. The page ends at its safe point, once no call on it is in flight, and its calls raise `page_memory_exceeded`, which is retryable.
settings.name: governor.browser.page_memory_cap

settings.description: How long a browser may hold no open page before it closes, each of its Sessions keeping its cookies and storage for the browser that replaces it: 5 minutes.
settings.name: governor.browser.recycle_idle

settings.description: How many pages a browser opens before it is recycled: 100. Recycled, it opens no new page, closes once its pages are done and is replaced, each of its Sessions keeping its cookies and storage.
settings.name: governor.browser.recycle_pages

settings.description: The most browser pages the engine's Resource governor admits open at once, across its Runs: 32.
settings.name: governor.browser_page.ceiling

settings.description: The fewest browser pages the engine's Resource governor keeps admitting at once, however loaded the machine: 1. Equal to `governor.browser_page.ceiling`, it fixes the concurrency there.
settings.name: governor.browser_page.floor

settings.description: The share of the Memory allowance in use, in percent, from which the engine's memory is critical: 95.
settings.name: governor.critical

settings.description: Whether the engine's Resource governor also judges the host's own memory, its memory in use against `governor.pressure` and `governor.critical` and the operating system's memory-pressure signal, and treats its pressure as the engine's: on. Off, the engine's own memory against its Memory allowance alone sets the level, as on a host whose other workloads are not the engine's to answer for.
settings.name: governor.host_memory

settings.description: The most HTTP and discovered-API fetches the engine's Resource governor admits at once, across its Runs: 200.
settings.name: governor.http.ceiling

settings.description: The fewest HTTP and discovered-API fetches the engine's Resource governor keeps admitting at once, however loaded the machine: 1. Equal to `governor.http.ceiling`, it fixes the concurrency there.
settings.name: governor.http.floor

settings.description: Whether the engine's own memory may be backed by the operating system's transparent huge pages: off, so the allocator reserves no memory the engine never touches, and the engine's resident memory is smaller. On, huge pages may back it, which is faster for some workloads and holds more memory. Read once, when the engine starts, on Linux; elsewhere it changes nothing. The browsers and other programs the engine starts keep the state the engine itself was started with either way.
settings.name: governor.huge_pages

settings.description: How long the engine's memory may stay critical with its concurrency at the floor before the Resource governor reaches its last resort, when a Daemon's `/readyz` fails: 60 s.
settings.name: governor.last_resort_after

settings.description: The most memory, in bytes, the engine and its children may use, as its Memory allowance when it is tighter than the process's own cgroup limit, its Windows Job object's limit or half of physical memory; unset by default. Each sample reads it from the engine's settings: the engine's own write (`config.user_write`, `config.policy_write`) is seen at the next sample, a hand edit at the engine's next read of the file, by the next Run's start at the latest.
settings.name: governor.memory_allowance

settings.description: The most model calls the engine's Resource governor admits at once, across its Runs: 16.
settings.name: governor.model_call.ceiling

settings.description: The fewest model calls the engine's Resource governor keeps admitting at once, however loaded the machine: 1. Equal to `governor.model_call.ceiling`, it fixes the concurrency there.
settings.name: governor.model_call.floor

settings.description: The share of the Memory allowance in use, in percent, from which the engine is under pressure and its Resource governor lowers its concurrency; also the CPU and Tokio workers' busy share from which they hold it: 85.
settings.name: governor.pressure

settings.description: The share, in percent, of each kind's concurrency one Run may hold at once, at least one: 100. An Operator policy cap bounds every Run's share.
settings.name: governor.run_share

settings.description: How often the engine's Resource governor reads memory, CPU and Tokio saturation, sizes its concurrency and sends `engine.system_info`: every second.
settings.name: governor.sample_interval

settings.description: How many worker threads run the engine's async tasks: 2, a whole number of at least 1, or `per_core` for one a core. A crawl's parsing runs on threads of its own, one a core at most, so few workers keep its memory low without slowing it. Read once, when the engine starts.
settings.name: governor.worker_threads

oneOf.description: This many threads.
One thread a core.

settings.description: Where a site reads the key directory of an `identified` Session's key, sent with each signed request as `Signature-Agent`, in the string form Cloudflare accepts: the `https://` origin that serves `goodfetch signing-key directory`'s output at `/.well-known/http-message-signatures-directory`, such as `https://bot.example`, or an inline `data:application/http-message-signatures-directory;base64,` directory. None by default; an `identified` Session needs it, with `identified.signing_key`. Set where a Session that is not `identified` opens, `setting_not_applicable`; inherited, it yields to the Access mode. A Label refuses it with `setting_not_applicable`.
settings.name: identified.signature_agent

value.description: Where a site reads the key directory: an `https://` or `http://` URL of the origin that serves it at `/.well-known/http-message-signatures-directory`, or an inline `data:application/http-message-signatures-directory;base64,` directory.

settings.description: The Secret reference of the Ed25519 key an `identified` Session signs each of its requests with (Web Bot Auth), such as `env:BOT_KEY`: never a value. It resolves to the key as a private JSON Web Key (`kty` `OKP`, `crv` `Ed25519`, with `d` and `x`), resolved once when the Session opens and never written to a log, a trace, a process's arguments or a file; a rotated key is read by the next Session. None by default; an `identified` Session needs it, with `identified.signature_agent`. Set where a Session that is not `identified` opens, `setting_not_applicable`; inherited, it yields to the Access mode. Set only by the program's own code, configuration and an Operator policy: a Recipe may expose it but never sets it, and a Client acting for a model is refused with `setting_locked`. A Label refuses it with `setting_not_applicable`.
settings.name: identified.signing_key
