settings.description: Whether a Session's pages hide, on the live page, the elements the Filter lists' cosmetic rules match: `auto` (the default) and `always` hide them through a style sheet the site cannot see on Chromium, in every frame and every new document; `off` leaves the live page as served. When the guard finds an action's target hidden, it lifts the rule for the Session and acts. Extracted content has the elements removed whatever this says.
settings.name: live_view.hiding

settings.description: How many log files an engine process keeps where `log.output` is `file`, the one it writes included: 5, so a Daemon's logs stay under about 50 MiB. The oldest goes at each rotation. A process other than the Daemon writes a set of files of its own, and at its start keeps as many of its executable's sets, its own included, the ones written last. Read when the process starts; set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.
settings.name: log.file.max_files

settings.description: The size, in bytes, at which an engine process's log file rotates where `log.output` is `file`: 10 MiB. A file holds at most this much and one line more. Read when the process starts; set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.
settings.name: log.file.max_size

settings.description: How an engine process writes its logs on stderr, or on stdout under `daemon run`: `text`, lines for a person reading a terminal, or `json`, JSON lines. Unset, the logs are text on stderr and JSON lines on stdout under `daemon run`; a log file holds JSON lines whatever it says. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.
settings.name: log.format

settings.description: Which of its logs an engine process writes: `info`, the default, which logs state changes only (a Run started, resumed or stopped, a domain backing off, a storage level changing, a Daemon draining) and never one line per request, or any `tracing` filter directive, such as `warn` or `info,goodfetch::rpc=debug`. Read when the process starts; set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.
settings.name: log.level

settings.description: Where an engine process writes its logs beside stderr: `stdout`, JSON lines for the platform to collect and rotate, `file`, JSON lines in its own files of the Goodfetch home's log folder, rotated at `log.file.max_size` and kept to `log.file.max_files`, or `none`. Unset, it is `stdout` under `daemon run`, `file` for every other Daemon and `none` for an Attached engine, whose logs go to its Client as log events; `stdout` on an Attached engine, whose stdout is its protocol, fails with `setting_not_applicable`. Read when the process starts; set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.
settings.name: log.output

settings.description: The most decoded bytes of one body the engine itself reads: a page `request`'s response, a kept response, an Operator-configured endpoint's reply. Never a download, which the disk governor bounds. 64 MiB (67108864) by default; set for a connection or a Run. A longer body fails the call with `response_limit_exceeded`.
settings.name: network.max_body_size

settings.description: The most decoded bytes per received byte of a body the engine reads, once its decoded bytes pass 1 MiB, so a decompression bomb is stopped as it expands. 100 by default; set for a connection or a Run. A body past it fails the call with `response_limit_exceeded`.
settings.name: network.max_decompression_ratio

settings.description: The most bytes of one line a Connection to a listener that takes a token may send before its `hello` is accepted, up to the 16 MiB (16777216) of any message: 64 KiB (65536) by default, many times any `hello`. A longer line closes the Connection unanswered as soon as it passes the limit, without being decoded, and the refusal is logged and recorded as `hello_too_large`. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.
settings.name: network.max_hello_size

settings.description: The deepest nesting of arrays and objects in JSON the engine parses from outside, from 0 to 1024: 128 by default; set for a connection or a Run. Deeper JSON fails the call with `response_limit_exceeded`.
settings.name: network.max_json_depth

settings.description: Host names mapped to addresses before any lookup, in the engine's resolver and in Chromium, each address still checked by ADR 0017's resolved-address rule. Empty by default; an Operator policy can lock it.
settings.name: network.resolve

settings.description: Where `daemon run`, the foreground Daemon, serves its ops listener, as `host:port`: `/livez` and `/readyz` answer a status and no body to anyone, and `/metrics`, Prometheus' text, only with the ops token, the `ops.token` file of the major's folder, as a bearer token. Unset by default: no ops listener and no Prometheus export. Any address, so a cluster's probes and scrapers reach it; a request whose `Host` is a name other than `localhost`, or that carries an `Origin`, is refused. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy, or for `daemon run` through `GOODFETCH_OPS_ADDRESS`.
settings.name: ops.address

settings.description: Where an Attached engine that runs its Runs itself serves an ops listener, as a loopback `host:port` such as `127.0.0.1:9465`: `/livez` and `/readyz` answer a status and no body, and `/metrics`, Prometheus' text, only with the ops token, the `ops.token` file of the major's folder, as a bearer token; its `goodfetch_counted_work_total` gives the engine's Counted work, such as the CDP commands it sent and the requests it paused. Unset by default: no ops listener, and the engine keeps no meter for one. An Attached engine in the per-install layout hands its Runs to the Daemon, whose `ops.address` serves them, and opens none. One address serves one engine: a second engine started with it fails to start.
settings.name: ops.attached_address

settings.description: The OTLP/HTTP endpoint an engine process sends its OpenTelemetry events to, such as `http://localhost:4318/v1/logs`: today the Audit log's entries, while `audit.otlp` is on. Unset, the default, sends nothing, and nothing leaves the machine. Read when the process starts; set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.
settings.name: otlp.logs_endpoint

settings.description: The OTLP/HTTP endpoint `daemon run`, the foreground Daemon, exports its metrics to, in protobuf, every 60 seconds and once more as it exits: a full URL such as `http://collector:4318/v1/metrics`. Unset by default: nothing is exported (ADR 0043).
settings.name: otlp.metrics_endpoint

settings.description: The OTLP/HTTP endpoint an engine process exports its `tracing` spans to, such as `http://localhost:4318/v1/traces`; unset, the default, exports nothing, and nothing leaves the machine. The spans cover each run, page and CDP command, with glossary IDs and bounded values as fields and a URL as its origin. Span names, span fields and the engine's targets are Experimental: a minor may change them, and its release notes list the change. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.
settings.name: otlp.traces_endpoint

settings.description: Whether a Run sharing Politeness takes each key's Delegation: while no other engine of the user uses a key, its engine keeps the key's Permits and state in memory, each Permit with no transaction on the Politeness file, and writes to the file at once what a site asked (a 429, a `Retry-After`, a backoff, a halved ceiling, a new Crawl-delay). Another engine that needs the key recalls it, and one whose holder is gone reclaims it, its delay counted from the reclaim. `false` takes and gives back each Permit in transactions of the file, unless the Run's engine already holds the key's Delegation for another Run: the Permit then comes from memory too, so the key's limits hold across both Runs. Ignored at `politeness.sharing: run`.
settings.name: politeness.delegation

settings.description: How many page navigations may be in flight at once through one proxy endpoint and credential, counted across every run of the user that shares Politeness, each redirect hop of a page's main frame counted, a program's own navigation included (a page's other requests and `page.request` are not counted): a run sends one only while that combined count is below its own value and below the ceiling the proxy's own refusals taught. At least 1; none by default, for no cap.
settings.name: politeness.proxy.concurrency

settings.description: How many page navigations a second may start through one proxy endpoint and credential, counted across every run of the user that shares Politeness, each redirect hop of a page's main frame counted, a program's own navigation included (a page's other requests and `page.request` are not counted): a run starts one only once a second divided by its own value has passed since the last start there by any sharing run. None by default.
settings.name: politeness.proxy.rate

settings.description: How a Run shares Politeness with the other runs of its user: `shared` with every engine of the user (through the Politeness store when one is configured, else on the machine), `per_daemon` on the machine only, ignoring a store, or `run` for Politeness of its own. Anything but `shared` is listed in the Run's result.
settings.name: politeness.sharing

settings.description: The hosts the Session reaches without its proxy, as Playwright's `bypass`: a comma-separated list such as `.example.com, chromium.org`, a leading dot naming a domain's subdomains. None by default: every request goes through `proxy.server`. Set as `proxy.server` is.
settings.name: proxy.bypass

settings.description: The country, an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code such as `US`, a Session's proxy exit is in. None by default: any country the provider offers. A country the provider does not offer for the Session's proxy kind is refused with `setting_invalid` when the Session opens. A Recipe never sets it (`setting_locked`).
settings.name: proxy.country

value.description: An ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, such as `US`.

settings.description: The proxy kind a Session's proxy is drawn from, `datacenter`, `isp`, `residential` or `mobile`: the provider's default when unset, for `list` the kind of its first server. A kind the provider does not offer is refused with `setting_invalid` when the Session opens. A Recipe may set it; a Client acting for a model is refused with `setting_locked`, since the kinds' prices differ by an order of magnitude and the person pays.
settings.name: proxy.kind

settings.description: The Secret reference of the password the Session gives `proxy.server` with `proxy.username`, such as `env:PROXY_PASSWORD`: never a value, resolved when the Session opens and never written to a log, a trace, a process's arguments or a file. None by default. Set as `proxy.server` is.
settings.name: proxy.password

settings.description: The Proxy provider each Session of the Run, or the Session it is set on, draws its one proxy from when it opens, fixed for the Session's life: `bright_data`, `oxylabs` or `apify`, whose adapters build the provider's sticky-session username from the account in `proxy.providers.<name>` and ask for the provider's longest sticky lifetime, or `list`, the user's own servers in `proxy.providers.list.servers`. None by default. A Session that resolves both `proxy.server` and `proxy.provider` is refused with `setting_invalid`. Set as `proxy.server` is: a Recipe may expose it but never sets it, and a Client acting for a model is refused with `setting_locked`.
settings.name: proxy.provider

settings.description: What each Proxy provider takes, by name, such as `proxy.providers.list`: `username`, the account's; `password`, a Secret reference resolved when a Session opens; `endpoint`, the provider's proxy URL in place of its public one (`http://brd.superproxy.io:33335` for `bright_data`, `http://pr.oxylabs.io:7777` for `oxylabs`, `http://proxy.apify.com:8000` for `apify`), an `http://`, `socks5://` or `socks5h://` URL, never `https://`, which the Session's loopback relay speaks no TLS to; `servers`, for `list` only, the user's own proxies, each a table of `server` (an `http://`, `socks5://` or `socks5h://` URL), `kind` and an optional `country`; `zones`, for `bright_data` only, the name of each proxy kind's zone as its customer named it, such as `{ residential = "residential_proxy1" }`, a kind it leaves out being the zone of the kind's own name, and the entry's `password` every zone's; and `price`, the price of a GB (10^9 bytes) through the provider, such as `5 USD`, which a currency Limit on `proxy_bytes` charges: under such a Limit a Session of an unpriced provider, or one priced in another currency, is refused with `setting_invalid`. Empty by default. Set only in an Operator policy and user and project configuration: a Recipe's or a run's value is `setting_locked`, so no Client lowers a price, and so is a project configuration's entry that names a `price`, which only user configuration and an Operator policy set, since a currency Limit trusts it.
settings.name: proxy.providers

password.description: The Secret reference of the account's password, such as `env:PROXY_PASSWORD`.

price.description: The price of a GB (10^9 bytes) through it, as an amount and its currency.

servers.description: The user's own servers, for `list` only.

zones.description: The zone of each proxy kind, for `bright_data` only: a kind left out is the zone of its own name.

settings.description: The proxy every request of the Session goes through, as Playwright's `server`: an `http://`, `https://`, `socks5://` or `socks5h://` URL with a host and a port, such as `http://proxy.example:3128`. None by default: the machine's own address. Set on a Run, every Session of it takes it; set in `run.new_session`'s `settings`, that Session alone; a page or a request has no proxy of its own, so the address a site sees never changes under the same cookies. A URL carrying credentials and `socks4` are refused with `setting_invalid`: give the credentials as `proxy.username` and `proxy.password`. Set only by the program's own code, configuration and an Operator policy: a Recipe may expose it but never sets it, and a Client acting for a model is refused with `setting_locked`, since whoever sets it receives `proxy.password`. On Chromium, a SOCKS5 proxy's credentials go through a loopback relay the engine opens for the Session.
settings.name: proxy.server

value.description: A proxy URL, `http://`, `https://`, `socks5://` or `socks5h://`, with a host and an optional port and never credentials, such as `http://proxy.example:3128`.

settings.description: How long, in milliseconds, a Session asks its provider to keep its proxy exit: the provider's longest when unset. A Session that outlives it is named by the Run report's `proxy_exit_may_change` warning; the engine never looks the exit up. A `list` server's exit never changes.
settings.name: proxy.sticky_lifetime

settings.description: The username the Session gives `proxy.server`, as Playwright's `username`. None by default. Set as `proxy.server` is.
settings.name: proxy.username

settings.description: How long the engine's HTTP transports let a connection attempt to one of a host's addresses run before they start the next one beside it: 250 ms, RFC 8305's Connection Attempt Delay. An attempt that fails starts the next at once.
settings.name: resolver.attempt_delay

settings.description: How long the engine's HTTP transports wait for a host's IPv6 addresses once its IPv4 addresses arrived first, before they start connecting over IPv4: 50 ms, RFC 8305's Resolution Delay.
settings.name: resolver.resolution_delay

settings.description: Write the Run's changes once they hold this many bytes of rows. This bounds the memory that changes not yet written take.
settings.name: run_state.batch.bytes

oneOf.description: Attempts, milliseconds or bytes, by the key, at which a batch is sealed.
No batch is sealed by this threshold.

settings.description: Write the Run's changes at least this often. A crash loses at most about this much work.
settings.name: run_state.batch.interval

oneOf.description: Attempts, milliseconds or bytes, by the key, at which a batch is sealed.
No batch is sealed by this threshold.

settings.description: Write the Run's changes once this many attempts have ended since the last batch. Lower loses less to a crash and writes more often.
settings.name: run_state.batch.pages

oneOf.description: Attempts, milliseconds or bytes, by the key, at which a batch is sealed.
No batch is sealed by this threshold.

settings.description: Write each attempt's claim before its fetch and its outcome before anything is told outside, as its own batch. Slowest, and a crash then loses only the attempts in flight.
settings.name: run_state.batch.per_attempt

settings.description: Which batches reach the disk before the next one starts. `each` survives a power cut; `interval` syncs one batch per `run_state.commit_interval`; `never` survives a process crash only; `off` syncs nothing, so a crash discards the run file and the Run starts again.
settings.name: run_state.batch.sync

settings.description: How often `run_state.batch.sync: interval` syncs a batch, and an idle Run's last changes.
settings.name: run_state.commit_interval

settings.description: How a Run's state reaches the disk, its Durability level, each value a preset of `run_state.batch.*` and `run_state.commit_interval`: `batch`, the default, writes the Run's changes in Run-state batches, of 1,000 attempts, 1 s or 8 MiB, whichever comes first, each synced, so a crash or a power cut loses at most the last batch; `full` writes each attempt's claim and outcome as a synced batch of its own (`synchronous=FULL`, with `fullfsync` on macOS), so only the attempts in flight are lost; `fast` is `full` unsynced (`synchronous=NORMAL`): it survives a process crash only, since an OS crash or a power cut may roll back recent commits, possibly many, without damaging the run state; `periodic` is `fast` with one synced batch every `run_state.commit_interval`, so a power cut loses at most that interval of work; `off` writes as `batch` does and syncs nothing (`synchronous=OFF`), and a run file a crash or a power cut left is discarded when the Run is next started or resumed, so the Run starts again from nothing. A level unfolds into its preset's keys at the layer that set it: a key set at that layer or a higher one overrides the preset's value, and a lock on the level locks every key of its preset. At every level a clean stop writes and syncs everything, so a paused Run resumes. The run report's `weakened` names `off`, and each preset key whose value weakens the Run.
settings.name: run_state.durability

settings.description: The Secret reference of the key-encryption key that wraps each Run's data key. One set in a layer is resolved when a Run starts: a Run whose reference does not resolve is refused with `secret_unavailable`. Taken only from an Operator policy and user and project configuration. By default the OS keychain's `keychain:goodfetch/run-state-key`, or, on a host with no OS keychain, the encrypted local file's `secretfile:run-state-key`, which `config explain` shows as the default it chose; the engine makes the default's item, a random 256-bit key, where it is missing when a Run first seals a field. A Run's data key is stored only wrapped by this key, so a resume, such as of a Checkpoint moved to another machine, unwraps it with the key this setting names for the resume, which a Client may send in `run.resume`'s project configuration: one that gives no value fails the resume with `secret_unavailable`, one that does not open the data key with `run_key_mismatch`. The encrypted local file, `secrets/<name>.age` in Goodfetch home encrypted with age to the X25519 identity in `secrets/identity.txt`, a file only its owner may read, protects copies and backups of the home, not the value from another process of the same user.
settings.name: run_state.key_reference

settings.description: Where Runs keep their run state: `per_run`, the default, one SQLite file in each run folder; `per_install`, one database, `run-state.sqlite` in the per-major folder, holding every Run of the install and major and written by the Daemon alone, to which an Attached engine then hands its Runs. Export, import and Checkpoint give the same per-run file in both. Taken only from the machine's own layers, and read when the Daemon starts.

settings.description: The folder that holds the run folders, each named by its Run ID; by default the per-user, per-major data folder of the Goodfetch home.

settings.description: The most memory this Run's Frontier, Leases and changes not yet written may hold, in bytes. Past it, or under memory pressure, state already written leaves memory and is read back from the run file. 0 keeps the Frontier in the run file. A budget of 0 with `run_state.batch.pages`, `.interval` and `.bytes` all `none` is refused, since nothing would ever leave memory.
